title: Learning and the Emergence of Nonlinearity in Financial Markets
affiliations: Kellogg School of Management - Department of Finance, Yale School of Management and Northwestern University

detail.title: Learning and the Emergence of Nonlinearity in Financial Markets
detail.abstract:
Financial markets (and more generally the real economy) display a wide range of important nonlinearities. This paper focuses on stock returns, which are skewedleft – generating crashes – and whose volatility moves over time, is itself skewed, is strongly related to the level of prices, and displays long memory. This paper shows that such behavior is almost inevitable when prices are formed by investors acquiring information about the true, but latent, value of stocks. It studies a general model of filtering in which agents receive signals about the fundamental value of the stock market and dynamically update their beliefs (potentially with biases). When those beliefs are non-normal and investors believe crashes can happen, prices generically display the range of nonlinearities observed in the data. While the model does not explain where crashes come from, it shows that investors believing that prices can crash is sufficient to generate the rich higher-order dynamics observed empirically. In a simple calibration with iid shocks to fundamentals, the model fits well quantitatively, and regression-based tests support the model’s mechanism.

title: The Cost of State-Building: Evidence from Germany
affiliations: Northwestern University - Kellogg School of Management

detail.title: The Cost of State-Building: Evidence from Germany
detail.abstract:
I examine the potential of pro-development state (capacity) building projects to be coopted for repression. I leverage the natural experiment created by the differential build-up of capacity between formerly Prussian and formerly non-Prussian parts of unified Germany, and the radical policy shifts instigated by the Nazi regime. Across a geographical discontinuity, and across different stops of the same train transport to the East, I find that Prussian municipalities were significantly more efficient at deporting Germany's Jews. They were also better at providing public goods and at collecting taxes. Just before the Nazis came to power, Prussian municipalities also provided public goods more efficiently, but were not differentially involved with anti-Semitism. I show that democratic oversight and aspects of bureaucratic culture can mitigate the potential for future abuse of state building projects.

title: Progressive EV Policy at Constant Adoption Evidence from Norway
affiliations: Carl von Ossietzky University of Oldenburg

detail.title: Progressive EV Policy at Constant Adoption Evidence from Norway
detail.abstract: Norway’s electric vehicle (EV) incentives rapidly diffused new technology but concentrated benefits regressively: the top income decile captured ∼70% of welfare gains, while the bottom four received <3%. We analyze whether a revenue-neutral redesign could achieve similar aggregate adoption with improved equity. Using a discrete-choice demand model on 2010–2019 Norwegian vehicle markets, we simulate static and dynamic incometargeted tax and subsidy schedules subject to quantity and budget constraints. Statically, the equity–quantity trade-off is steep: a 1 percentage-point (pp) tax on the top decile requires roughly a 13.7 pp subsidy to the bottom half to hold quantities fixed, and subsidy caps— not the budget—bind. Targeting marginal adopters (deciles 3–5) is crucial; taxing the top decile at ∼ 3% and subsidizing D1-D5 at ∼ 15% raises the bottom 40% EV share from 2.7% to 5% while generating revenue. Dynamically, optimal policy paths diverge significantly under efficiency versus equity objectives. Efficiency favors front-loaded subsidies financed by delayed taxes; equity demands a smoother path, sacrificing adoption speed for distributional fairness. As the market matures, the fiscal cost of redistribution decreases significantly.

title: How Good is International Risk Sharing?  Stepping Outside the Shadow of the Welfare Theorems
affiliations: Princeton University, Harvard University and London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Economics

detail.title: How Good is International Risk Sharing?  Stepping Outside the Shadow of the Welfare Theorems
detail.abstract:
We revisit whether global output is (Pareto) efficiently distributed across countries over time. The efficient allocation of goods across regions requires that the relative marginal utilities of consumption across countries comoves with the relative costs of the country-specific consumption bundles. Standard approaches to evaluating this property exploit the Welfare Theorems and equate the observed real exchange rate with the social relative costs of consumption. Given the large literature documenting the disconnect between exchange rates, relative prices faced by consumers in a given market, and relative quantities consumed, we develop a methodology that measures relative costs that is robust to this disconnect. We find that relative consumption growth across regions is significantly more correlated with our computed shadow prices than it is with observed real exchange rates, suggesting an allocation closer to efficient risk sharing. Moreover, we provide a decentralization that matches observed prices and quantities, enabling us to rationalize the better implied risk sharing with the failure of the standard correlations. The decentralization involves a combination of segmented foreign exchange markets and pricing-to-market behavior in goods markets. The model implies that consumption allocations are insulated from excess fluctuations in the exchange rate via the equilibrium pricing behavior of exporters.

title: Monetary Policy Transmission in an Emerging Market: The Financial-Friction Channel VS The Interest-Rate Channel
affiliations: Banco de Mexico, Banco de Mexico and Georgetown University

detail.title: Monetary Policy Transmission in an Emerging Market: The Financial-Friction Channel VS The Interest-Rate Channel
detail.abstract: We provide the first micro-level evidence on monetary policy transmission in an emerging market (EM). Exploiting high-frequency identification and an exceptionally detailed dataset covering over 10 million firm-month observations of bank loans to private firms, we study how monetary policy affects credit in Mexico. Firms more affected by financial frictionsand thus frequently perceived as riskier, such as young firms, SMEs, and those with recent delinquencies-experience earlier, stronger, and more persistent reductions in credit after tightening, consistent with a financial-frictions channel. Firms producing durables also face larger declines, supporting an interest-rate channel. Contrary to the direction suggested by advanced-economy findings, however, the financial-frictions channel dominates the interestrate channel. Further evidence strengthens this result: (i) the dominance of the financial friction channel is strongest precisely for banks more pressed to diminish risk-taking; and (ii) transmission to regional employment growth is likewise stronger through financial frictions than through the interest-rate channel. Overall, the results underscore the distinctive nature of monetary policy transmission in EMs.

title: Feeling Rich or Looking Rich? Quantifying Self-Image and Social-Image Motives
affiliations: Cornell University, University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), Simon Fraser University (SFU) and Kindai University - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Feeling Rich or Looking Rich? Quantifying Self-Image and Social-Image Motives
detail.abstract: Preferences for status are typically attributed to two distinct channels: self-image, in which individuals derive utility from being richer than others, and social-image, in which individuals value being seen as richer by others. While both channels are believed to be at play, little is known about their relative importance. We address this gap using a hypothetical discrete choice experiment. Our findings indicate that social-image tends to carry greater weight than self-image, with substantial heterogeneity in the strength of these preferences across individuals and domains.

title: Elections and Political Investment
affiliations: Tulane University, Department of Economics

detail.title: Elections and Political Investment
detail.abstract:
Elections select officeholders and policies, but they also signal to political actors where to invest their time and money. This paper presents a framework for understanding these effects, in which political investors (e.g., donors, activists) allocate resources where expected political fundamentals favor their party. Investors possess idiosyncratic local knowledge but also public information in the form of recent election results. These signals are complementary: where local knowledge is good, even the narrowest vote-share majorities can align beliefs and concentrate investment. I apply this framework to the changing political geography of the United States between 1940 and 1972, when urban and minority areas came into play for the Democratic Party. A regression discontinuity design based on close presidential elections shows that counties narrowly won by Democrats saw pronounced increases in Democratic local officeholding and voter support in subsequent election periods. This does not reflect direct impacts of presidential elections on local offices, but rather indirect shifts through political investment, including heightened activity in newspaper advertising, phone banking, and civil rights mobilization. Effects are concentrated in urban, Black, and union areas where dense organizational networks enhanced local political knowledge. Together, the findings show how elections organize political actors not only at the ballot box but through the information they convey.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Unconscious Intelligence: Exploring the I-Factor in Decision-Making
affiliations: , RheinMain University of Applied Sciences and

detail.title: Unconscious Intelligence: Exploring the I-Factor in Decision-Making
detail.abstract: Is there an overarching ability within us that helps us solve problems unconsciously and which is more pronounced in some people than in others? This study investigates the potential existence of an "I-factor" (Intuitive factor), analogous to the established G-factor (general intelligence). We build on Cognitive-Experiential Self-Theory (CEST) and assume that there are two interacting cognitive systems (i.e., an unconscious, heuristic, fast, and affective system and a conscious, slow, and rational system) which guides our decision. Using a multi-method approach, a total of 6,912 decisions were recorded from 61 students in three implicit tests, while skin conductance was simultaneously recorded to measure somatic markers. Somatic markers are reactions of the sympathetic nervous system (the flight-or-fight-system), whereby earlier studies show that before individuals have consciously understood the rules of a cognitive test, their sympathetic nervous system already reacts appropriately (i.e., it shows stronger reactions before incorrect decisions). The results provide evidence that individuals who show advantageous somatic markers (i.e. sympathetic reactions are stronger to wrong decisions than to right ones) in one implicit test also show similar markers in other tests. Our results also show that individuals with advantageous somatic markers are more likely to be able to explicitly name the rules underlying the implicit tests, which few can do. This highlights the interaction between the two systems. Based on our findings and existing research, we propose a modified form of CEST, which aims to motivate further research.

title: Non-monotonic Equilibria in Random Signaling with Unobservable Effort
affiliations: University of International Business and Economics (UIBE) - School of International Trade and Economics and Peking University

detail.title: Non-monotonic Equilibria in Random Signaling with Unobservable Effort
detail.abstract: In this paper, we consider a two-stage model of random signaling with unobservable effort. In the first stage, the privately informed sender chooses an action to influence the distribution of the signal sent to the receiver. In the second stage, the receiver only observes a realization of the signal, not the sender's type or action, and then responds optimally. We show that non-monotonic equilibria, where middle-type senders behave differently from those at the extremes, may emerge. The results are driven by the endogenous interaction between unobservable effort and signal randomness, without requiring external information sources, multi-dimensional types, particular preference structures, behavioral assumptions, or dynamic considerations.

title: Natural Disasters and Perceived Returns to Education
affiliations: World Bank Group and World Bank - Development Research Group (DECRG)

detail.title: Natural Disasters and Perceived Returns to Education
detail.abstract: The occurrence of unexpected shocks, such as natural disasters, that destroy physical capital could affect the perception of returns to investment in human capital. This paper tests this hypothesis using a survey conducted in Mozambique while Cyclone Idai hit the country in March 2019. A difference-in-difference approach is used to compare the households interviewed before and after the cyclone occurrence, as well as the households that were directly affected by the cyclone, through destruction, injuries, and deaths. The results indicate that households affected by major shocks report higher perceived returns to completing primary education.

title: Tax-Induced Spatial Substitution and the Price Elasticity of Fuel Demand
affiliations: University of Oxford - Center for Business Taxation and Universidad Nacional de Educacion a Distancia (UNED) - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Tax-Induced Spatial Substitution and the Price Elasticity of Fuel Demand
detail.abstract: This paper estimates the price elasticity of fuel demand in the presence of spatial variations in fuel taxes. Using variations in fuel tax rates across Spanish regions, we document two main findings. First, we identify substantial spatial substitution in diesel sales, with an elasticity of -9 near regional borders. Second, we demonstrate that failing to account for such spatial substitution can lead to an overestimation of the price elasticity of fuel demand. Ignoring spatial substitution yields an elasticity of about -3, whereas diesel demand becomes inelastic when spatial substitution is accounted for. Our findings highlight the relevance of spatial substitution in the observed responses of fuel demand to unilateral tax changes, and suggest that localized environmental policies aimed at reducing CO2 emissions may be less effective than previously assumed.

title: The Materiality of AI: A Qualitative Analysis of Water Dependencies across Models, Data Centers, and Semiconductor Supply Chains
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: The Materiality of AI: A Qualitative Analysis of Water Dependencies across Models, Data Centers, and Semiconductor Supply Chains
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly portrayed as a driver of sustainability transitions, yet its material infrastructures and implications for water availability remain insufficiently understood. This study contributes to debates on the materiality of digital technologies by synthesizing evidence on AI’s water footprint and examining how technological, institutional, and political-economic factors shape water consumption across its life cycle. Drawing on a systematic literature review, corporate sustainability reports, and expert perspectives, we analyze water dependencies in three domains: semiconductor fabrication, data-center operation (training and inference), and energy generation for AI workloads. The review shows that while AI’s global water footprint is substantial, its local impacts are highly uneven—exacerbating water stress and conflicts in some regions while remaining marginal in others. Beyond quantification, the analysis identifies major barriers to water-efficient AI, including limited data transparency and inconsistent metrics, weak regulation and economic incentives, low visibility and diffusion of best practices, market concentration, and insufficiently transparent global supply chains. If left unaddressed, these structural barriers risk constraining the development of more water-efficient AI and, amid growing global water stress, could exacerbate resource conflicts and regional inequalities. By foregrounding water as a critical dimension of AI’s materiality, this study advances understanding of the environmental justice and sustainability challenges of digital infrastructures.

title: Investigating the circular transition of the sheep supply chain: state of the art and future perspectives at the local level

detail.title: Investigating the circular transition of the sheep supply chain: state of the art and future perspectives at the local level
detail.abstract: The sheep supply chain represents a relevant component of the agro-livestock and industrial system, not only in food production but also for its socio-economic and environmental functions especially in rural areas. These territories, often mountainous, semi-arid, or otherwise disadvantaged, depend on sheep farming as one of the few viable productive activities. Currently, the sheep sector is experiencing a structural crisis caused by low profitability, declining consumption, foreign competition, and the progressive depopulation of inland areas that undermine both its economic and social sustainability, leading to negative territorial consequences such as pasture abandonment and biodiversity loss.The article, as one of the first outcomes of the MAX-SHEEP research project, aims to contribute to this topic investigating the current features of the sheep supply chain and identifying pathways for its re-development, taking advantage of the opportunities proposed by the Circular Economy paradigm, especially those suitable at the local level. The study was conducted through a scientific and technical literature research, which examines: the current structure and the strategic role of the sheep sector; its main environmental impacts; existing solutions and indicators for fostering and assessing circular transition potential.Results show that, although the sheep sector exerts considerable environmental pressure, it holds significant potential for a circular transition. The adoption of circular practices, such as waste valorization, resource efficiency, and cross-sectoral collaboration, could enhance sustainability. However, successful implementation requires context-specific strategies that respect the historical, socio-economic, and territorial features, ensuring that circular solutions identified are both feasible and impactful at the local level.

title: Revealing Tax Evasion: Experimental Evidence from a Representative Survey of Indonesian Firms
affiliations: World Bank,  and World Bank

detail.title: Revealing Tax Evasion: Experimental Evidence from a Representative Survey of Indonesian Firms
detail.abstract: Measuring tax evasion by firms is notoriously difficult: direct questions yield biased responses while administrative data captures only detected violations. This paper examines the pervasiveness of tax evasion in Indonesia and the characteristics associated with non-compliance through a randomized, double-list experiment embedded in a nationally representative survey of 2,955 registered firms that preserves anonymity. The results reveal that around a quarter of firms indirectly admit to evading tax, which is equivalent to a revenue loss of two percent of GDP.  Firms that do not export, face informal sector competition, and believe tax administration is a major obstacle are the most likely to evade taxes. These findings help inform tax authorities, which face substantial challenges in estimating levels of tax evasion and identifying non-compliant taxpayers. This study provides the first validation that double-list experiments reliably measure sensitive organizational behaviors and offers representative estimates of firm tax evasion in a major middle-income country.

title: Economic and Environmental Consequences of Future Technological Progress in Buildings
affiliations: Boston University, Boston University, Northeastern University (USA) and Schneider Electric

detail.title: Economic and Environmental Consequences of Future Technological Progress in Buildings
detail.abstract: We use a computable general equilibrium (CGE) model integrating bottom-up technology detail to investigate the economic and environmental consequences of adoption of the building of the future: updating a portion of the aggregate building stock with advanced building technologies that are less energy- and carbon-intensive but more capital-intensive. Targeting the 10-year stock of retrofit and new vintages of six building archetypes in 13 economic sectors across 10 advanced economies in the year 2030, adoption of the building of the future could reduce building archetypes' electricity consumption by up to 13% and their direct carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions by up to 17%. But because the archetypes considered in this analysis make up a relatively small fraction of aggregate emissions and economic activity, building technology improvements' economywide abatement and cost impacts are on the order of a 0.9-3.2% reduction in emissions and a 0.02-0.21% GDP loss. Although building technologies reduce emissions by eliminating a portion of fossil fuel demand, roughly two thirds of their abatement can be traced to upstream impacts on electric power. Despite sizable opportunities to reduce emissions from dwellings, retrofit and new office archetypes and new retail archetypes are often the most cost-effective sources of abatement. Our results suggest that the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada are regions where adoption of the building of the future is likely to be relatively cost-effective as a climate change mitigation strategy.

title: Thresholds and Asymmetries: The Non-Linear Effects of Digital Finance and Institutional Quality on Financial Inclusion in SADC
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Thresholds and Asymmetries: The Non-Linear Effects of Digital Finance and Institutional Quality on Financial Inclusion in SADC
detail.abstract: The relationship between digital finance and financial inclusion is fundamentally shaped by a country's institutional quality. This study investigates the non-linear effects of digital finance and institutional quality on financial inclusion in the Southern African Development Community (SADC). Using a balanced panel of 15 countries from 2004 to 2022, we construct a composite Financial Inclusion Index and employ system GMM and robust panel estimators. The results reveal critical thresholds: digital finance boosts inclusion only after reaching a critical mass of adoption, while institutional quality exhibits diminishing and, at high levels, negative returns suggesting a risk of regulatory overreach. We also identify an inverted U-shaped relationship for digital literacy, indicating that its uneven distribution can exacerbate existing divides. Disaggregated analysis shows that lower-income economies benefit most from digital adoption, whereas higher-income economies rely more on institutional efficacy. We conclude that financial inclusion is a contingent process, requiring policies tailored to a country's specific digital preparedness, institutional robustness, and income level

title: Global Fisheries: Socio-economic Impacts of Overfishing
affiliations: , , Minderoo Foundation, Minderoo Foundation and University of British Columbia (UBC) - Fisheries Economics Research Unit

detail.title: Global Fisheries: Socio-economic Impacts of Overfishing
detail.abstract: This study estimates global fisheries catch loss, i.e., the difference between the maximum sustainable yield (MSY) of a fish stock and its catch in the most recent year, arising from overfished fish stocks, and the associated socio-economic impacts. We focus on 482 fish stocks identified as ‘overfished’ in the 2021 Global Fishing Index, for which we estimate: (1) the potential catch loss (in tonnes); (2) the landed value (in USD) of catch loss; and (3) the number of jobs associated with catch loss worldwide. We estimated an annual catch loss of 10.7 million t globally for 2018, which translated to around USD 12.2 billion in potential lost landed value annually, and an estimated 668,500 in associated full time equivalent jobs. While it is unlikely for all commercial stocks in an ecosystem to simultaneously achieve MSY, our analysis indicates that restoring fish stocks to sustainable levels that support fishing at MSY could potentially lead to biological and socio-economic gains in all regions worldwide. As such, this study emphasises the urgent need to immediately rebuild overfished fish stocks to recoup economic and social benefits that are forgone with catch loss.

title: Options Traders, Short-Term Reversals, and Return Predictability
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Charlotte - Finance,  and Cambridge University

detail.title: Options Traders, Short-Term Reversals, and Return Predictability
detail.abstract: Customer option traders are sophisticated in exploiting short-term stock returnreversals and continuations. They possess information, corroborated by the tone ofsubsequent corporate filings, that enable them to identify stocks whose price declinesare excessive relative to near-term fundamentals. A trading strategy that tracks theirpositions earns significant abnormal daily returns, with even larger gains observed inthe options market. These profits arise from informed trading and retail copycat behavior,after controlling for other established explanations. Similar strategies basedon the trading of short sellers or average institutional investors do not yield profits.Overall, the evidence shows that customer option traders act as informed arbitrageurscontributing to market efficiency.

title: A Novel MIMO Multi-Gene Genetic Programming Approach for Interpretable NARX Models: an application to vehicle state estimation
affiliations: Federal University of Lavras, Federal University of Lavras, Federal University of Lavras, , Brock University and

detail.title: A Novel MIMO Multi-Gene Genetic Programming Approach for Interpretable NARX Models: an application to vehicle state estimation
detail.abstract: Identification of nonlinear dynamic systems requires simultaneous structure detection and parameter estimation, which becomes especially challenging for multi-ple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. We propose an evolutionary identification algorithm that combines genetic programming and genetic algorithms to obtain polynomial Nonlinear Autoregressive with Exogeneous inputs (NARX) models. The method performs regressor selection across a search space that is intractable for classical techniques and integrates structure detection with parameter estimation within a single optimization loop. We apply the method to vehicle dynamics modeling and present insights on using multiple shooting techniques during estimation, demonstrating the important role of the chosen prediction horizon in the identification process. Interpretable polynomial NARX models recovered terms consistent with known vehicle dynamics and achieved R2 values exceeding 0.90 on highly challenging datasets. The proposed approach yields particularly accurate estimates of lateral dynamics. Compared with other machine learning techniques, the proposed method produces substantially better predictive performance and clearer physical interpretability.

title: Green Energy and Income Inequality: Is There a Causal Effect?
affiliations: Deakin University,  and Deakin University, Chinese University of Hong Kong - Department of Economics

detail.title: Green Energy and Income Inequality: Is There a Causal Effect?
detail.abstract: To protect the environment, global efforts have been devoted to climate change issues, with a particular attention to renewable (or green) energy in both the production and consumption process. While green energy has undeniable benefits on the wellbeing of individuals, whether it may heighten or lessen the status of income inequality in an economy over time remains unknown. This paper attempts to shed some lights on this topic. To this end, a general-equilibrium model is considered in which green energy investment, funded by corporate taxes, serves as an output-scaling factor in manufacturing production. It is shown that in the short run, green energy yields a double dividend for the economy by improving social welfare and at the same time narrowing the income gap between skilled and unskilled labours. In the long run, green energy may promote firm entry, which enlarges the income disparity and hence repudiates the short run gains. Using data from 65 countries in the period from 1960 to 2022, we show that a one percent increase in green energy investment enhances GDP growth by about 0.032% and reduces income inequality by about 0.012% in the short run. In the long run, green energy investment reduces income inequality in advanced economies but with a much smaller magnitude versus the short run, thus confirming the theoretical predictions. Results provide a strong case for governments around the world to consider the distributive effects of green energy on the economy, an area that has been neglected thus far.

title: Modeling Bank Systemic Risk of Emerging Markets under Geopolitical Shocks: Empirical Evidence from BRICS Countries
affiliations: Texas A&M International University

detail.title: Modeling Bank Systemic Risk of Emerging Markets under Geopolitical Shocks: Empirical Evidence from BRICS Countries
detail.abstract: The growing economic influence of the BRICS nations requires risk models that capture complex, long-term dynamics. This paper introduces the Bank Risk Interlinkage with Dynamic Graph and Event Simulations (BRIDGES) framework, which analyzes systemic risk based on the level of information complexity (zero-order, first-order, and second-order). BRIDGES utilizes the Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) distance to construct a dynamic network for 551 BRICS banks based on their strategic similarity, using zero-order information such as annual balance sheet data from 2008 to 2024. It then employs first-order information, including trends in risk ratios, to detect shifts in banks’ behavior. A Temporal Graph Neural Network (TGNN), as the core of BRIDGES, is deployed to learn network evolutions and detect second-order information, such as anomalous changes in the structural relationships of the bank network. To measure the impact of anomalous changes on network stability, BRIDGES performs Agent-Based Model (ABM) simulations to assess the banking system’s resilience to internal financial failure and external geopolitical shocks at the individual country level and across BRICS nations.Simulation results show that the failure of the largest institutions causes more systemic damage than the failure of the financially vulnerable or dynamically anomalous ones, driven by powerful panic effects. Compared to this “too big to fail” scenario, a geopolitical shock with correlated country-wide propagation causes more destructive systemic damage, leading to a near-total systemic collapse. It suggests that the primary threats to BRICS financial stability are second-order panic and large-scale geopolitical shocks, which traditional risk analysis models might not detect.

title: A Multivariate Bernoulli-Based Sampling Method for Multi-Label Data with Application to Meta-Research
affiliations: , Indiana University Bloomington,  and

detail.title: A Multivariate Bernoulli-Based Sampling Method for Multi-Label Data with Application to Meta-Research
detail.abstract: Datasets may contain observations with multiple labels. If the labels are not mutually exclusive, and if the labels vary greatly in frequency, obtaining a sample that includes sufficient observations with scarcer labels to make inferences about those labels, and which deviates from the population frequencies in a known manner, creates challenges. In this paper, we consider a multivariate Bernoulli distribution as our underlying distribution of a multi-label problem. We present a novel sampling algorithm that takes label dependencies into account. It uses observed label frequencies to estimate multivariate Bernoulli distribution parameters and calculate weights for each label combination. This approach ensures the weighted sampling acquires target distribution characteristics while accounting for label dependencies. We applied this approach to a sample of research articles from Web of Science labeled with 64 biomedical topic categories. We aimed to preserve category frequency order, reduce frequency differences between most and least common categories, and account for category dependencies. This approach produced a more balanced sub-sample, enhancing the representation of minority categories.

title: Machine Learning–Enhanced ARDL Modeling of SDG-7 Impacts on Long-Run Economic Stability
affiliations: Tsinghua University

detail.title: Machine Learning–Enhanced ARDL Modeling of SDG-7 Impacts on Long-Run Economic Stability
detail.abstract: This paper examines the long-term contribution of Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG-7)—affordable and clean energy—to economic stability based on a combination of traditional and modern machine learning methodologies. The study applies an Adaptive Regional Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to assess both the short-run changes and long-run elasticities connected to accessible energy, the use of renewable sources of power, and the inflow of external financial resources by using annual time-series data covering 1988-2023. The ARDL estimates demonstrate that the indicators of SDG-7 are significantly related to the macroeconomic expansion long-term, which demonstrates the importance of effective electricity availability and renewable generation capacity in their sustenance. To enhance the solidity of the ARDL results, machine learning methods are employed as validation measures, specifically the Random Forest (RF) or the Granular Additive Models (GAMs) methods. The consistency and predictability of the econometric outcomes were also verified, as the ML models have an accuracy of 93.4% on six performance metrics. The connectivity diagnostics also reveal the existence of unidirectional and bidirectional linkages between energy-related variables. Overall, the study is of high empirical value, which makes SDG-7 one of the main approaches to sustainable development, particularly in emerging and small-scale economies.

title: A plug-and-play decay pruning method with smooth and self-rectifying properties
affiliations: Ningbo University, Ningbo University, , Ningbo University - Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and Ningbo University

detail.title: A plug-and-play decay pruning method with smooth and self-rectifying properties
detail.abstract: Current structured pruning methods often suffer from unavoidable information loss caused by abrupt structure removal, and their pruning decisions are frequently sub-optimal due to limited information during pruning. To address these issues, we introduce the Decay Pruning Method (DPM), a novel smooth pruning approach with a self-rectifying mechanism. DPM consists of two key components: (i) Smooth Pruning: it conducts a multi-step smooth pruning process, gradually reducing the redundant structures to zero, thereby alleviating abrupt network changes and improving information retention; (ii) Self-Rectifying: it further enhances the pruning process by adaptively rectifying sub-optimal pruning decisions based on gradient information, ensuring more reliable and adaptive pruning outcomes. Owing to its simple and effective design, DPM offers plug-and-play compatibility, enabling seamless integration into diverse existing pruning frameworks. Applied to three representative methods—OTOv2, Depgraph, and Gate Decorator—DPM consistently demonstrates strong effectiveness and generalizability. Our evaluations span both convolutional and Vision Transformer architectures on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet, showing stable accuracy improvements and additional reductions in FLOPs compared to the original methods.

title: Progressive Diffusion for Single Image Dehazing
affiliations: Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology and Dalian University of Technology

detail.title: Progressive Diffusion for Single Image Dehazing
detail.abstract: Single image dehazing remains a challenging task, particularly under dense haze conditions where much of the scene information is severely obscured. Existing approaches, including those based on convolutional neural networks and vision transformers, often suffer from content degradation and color distortion in such scenarios. Recently, denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) have emerged as powerful generative frameworks, showing promise for restoration tasks due to their ability to synthesize fine details. However, most diffusion-based dehazing methods suffer from color shift artifacts, likely due to high model variance in estimating the spatial mean of the score function, which hinders global color consistency during generation.To address these challenges, we propose a novel perceptually enhanced diffusion model tailored for single image dehazing. Our method introduces a progressive diffusion strategy that gradually increases the image resolution during training, allowing the model to focus on coarse-to-fine restoration. We design a progressive backbone architecture that evolves with the input scale, enabling stable and efficient learning across resolutions. In addition, we incorporate a consistency-preserving batch statistics module to mitigate color shift by maintaining coherent feature distributions across diffusion steps.Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach not only recovers finer textures but also significantly improves perceptual color fidelity, achieving state-of-the-art performance in quantitative and visual comparisons.The code of PD-Dehaze is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/PD-Dehaze.

title: A note on adaptive conformal prediction for time series with structural breaks
affiliations: University College Dublin (UCD)

detail.title: A note on adaptive conformal prediction for time series with structural breaks
detail.abstract: Standard conformal prediction methods rely on the exchangeability assumption, which is violated in time series forecasting under non-stationary conditions. While recent approaches like Ensemble Batch Prediction Intervals (EnbPI) address serial dependence, they often exhibit slow adaptation to abrupt structural breaks, leading to significant loss of coverage. In this note, we propose an adaptive conformal inference framework that integrates a sequential change-point detection mechanism based on CUSUM statistics to dynamically reset the calibration window. We establish the asymptotic validity of the proposed method, proving that the conditional coverage gap converges to zero following a detected change-point. Numerical experiments on synthetic processes and real-world financial data demonstrate that our approach minimizes the detection delay and restores validity significantly faster than fixed-window baselines.

title: Corporate Investment and Stock Returns Under North Korea Threats
affiliations: KDI School of Public Policy and Management, Korea National Defense University and Incheon National University

detail.title: Corporate Investment and Stock Returns Under North Korea Threats
detail.abstract: We study how geopolitical risk from North Korea affects South Korean firms’ investment and stock returns. We construct a novel monthly GPRNK index from news articles, which spikes during nuclear tests or military confrontations and falls during summits. Heightened GPRNK reduces corporate investment and stock returns, with larger effects for capital-intensive, and geopolitically exposed firms. By contrast, firms with higher labor flexibility are less affected. Local projection estimates show that investment declines are persistent. These results highlight both real options and Oi–Hartman–Abel channels in the transmission of geopolitical risk.

title: Regimes of distributive conflict and inflation spirals
affiliations: ,  and Catholic University of Milan

detail.title: Regimes of distributive conflict and inflation spirals
detail.abstract: In this paper, we assess the relationship between income distribution and price dynamics, focusing on the role of distributive conflict between labor and capital in the U.S. economy over the period 1960–2023. We employ a spectral decomposition in both the frequency and time–frequency domains to document how different distributive–inflation configurations have coexisted and shifted over these six decades. We complement the empirical analysis with a tractable nonlinear disequilibrium model in which inflation emerges endogenously from evolving wage–price and profit–price spirals. Structural parameters act as bifurcation triggers, determining whether inflationary pressures are wage-led or profit-led. By isolating the conflict channels and their dynamic feedback, we highlight how shifts in bargaining power and markup claims can sustain persistent inflationary regimes, with implications for policies addressing the structural roots of inflation.

title: Verba Volant, Transcripta Manent What Corporate Earnings Calls Reveal About the AI Stock Rally
affiliations: , European Central Bank (ECB) and

detail.title: Verba Volant, Transcripta Manent What Corporate Earnings Calls Reveal About the AI Stock Rally
detail.abstract: This paper examines how firms’ exposure to generative AI affects financial performance, exploiting ChatGPT’s release. We propose a novel framework leveraging LLMs to analyze earnings call transcripts. Our method quantifies firms’ GenAI exposure and classifies sentiment as opportunity, adoption, or risk. Using panel econometric techniques, we assess the impact of GenAI exposure on S&P 500 firms’ financial performance over 2014-2023. We find that firms with early GenAI exposure saw stronger returns, though earnings expectations improved modestly. Panel regressions show that Early Exposed firms outperformed Laggards by around 0.26pp in quarterly excess returns for every 1pp increase in GenAI exposure, and Difference in-Differences estimates indicate 2.4pp higher average quarterly stock price gains. Investor reactions varied with the tone of GenAI discussions, suggesting markets valued signals of adoption more than opportunities.

title: PowerMarketSim: A Fundamental Market Model for Day-Ahead Price Formation with Heterogeneous Orders and Market Coupling
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: PowerMarketSim: A Fundamental Market Model for Day-Ahead Price Formation with Heterogeneous Orders and Market Coupling
detail.abstract: The transition of European day-ahead (DA) electricity markets to a 15-minute resolution introduces new price dynamics and operational requirements that existing modeling approaches struggle to capture. Statistical and machine-learning methods offer high predictive accuracy but lack interpretability and are unreliable under structural change. Fundamental models address these limitations but often simplify bidding behavior, interzonal constraints and unit-level resolution, limiting their ability to reproduce realistic price formation and the detailed dispatch patterns required for system-level analyses. This paper presents PowerMarketSim, a fundamental DA market model that applies Lagrangian relaxation to couple decentralized bidding with a detailed market-clearing process. The framework mirrors the actual market sequence: generation units optimize bids based on marginal costs, while the clearing algorithm determines order acceptance and zonal prices. The clearing problem is formulated as a mixed-integer optimization model that explicitly incorporates heterogeneous order types and congestion rents, capturing how bidding decisions and cross-border transmission constraints shape zonal price formation. Comparative analysis shows that simplified pricing approaches reproduce only average price levels and fail to reflect realistic temporal and structural price patterns. In contrast, PowerMarketSim reproduces observed price variability, highlights the influence of block orders on market outcomes and provides physically consistent dispatch results. The model bridges the gap between optimization-based market models and empirical price analysis, offering an interpretable and robust tool for studying DA price formation.

title: Artificial Neural Network Approach for Ultra-High Frequency Partial Discharge Localization in Mineral Oil Based on Time Difference of Arrival Datasets
affiliations: Universiti Putra Malaysia, Universiti Putra Malaysia, Universiti Putra Malaysia, Universiti Putra Malaysia, University Putra Malaysia and Universiti Tenaga Nasional

detail.title: Artificial Neural Network Approach for Ultra-High Frequency Partial Discharge Localization in Mineral Oil Based on Time Difference of Arrival Datasets
detail.abstract: This study presents a dataset generation procedure to train artificial neural networks (ANNs) for ultra-high frequency (UHF) partial discharge (PD) localization in an oil-filled tank. The datasets were generated from the time difference of arrival (TDOA) equations and augmented with samples that contain random deviations. The PD localization performance of the ANNs trained with the datasets was compared with the genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), bat algorithm (BA), artificial bee colony (ABC), and a non-iterative algorithm, based on the TDOAs of experimental UHF PD signals. A laboratory experiment was conducted where UHF PD signals were captured by 4 patch-type ultra-wideband antennas and then denoised by the variational mode decomposition (VMD) method. TDOAs were computed from both the original and denoised UHF PD signals through the First Peak Method (FPM) and the Cumulative Energy Method (CEM). For the original UHF PD signals, the FPM produces TDOAs with lower mean absolute errors (MAEs) than the CEM, and the opposite holds for the denoised UHF PD signals. Among the tested PD localization algorithms, the trained ANNs consistently provide the highest PD localization accuracy, with average computation time between 36.83 ms and 42.89 ms.

title: Connectedness and risk transmission across artificial intelligence industries
affiliations: University of Economics in Bratislava, University of Economics in Bratislava and University of Economics in Bratislava

detail.title: Connectedness and risk transmission across artificial intelligence industries
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a key innovation in the global economy, with AI-related equities becoming major drivers of the recent stock market upswing. Yet, the internal dynamics and heterogeneity within the AI sector remain largely unexplored. We address this gap by analysing the connectedness and risk transmission among four AI industries: hardware manufacturers, cloud providers, application developers, and AI-intensive BigTech firms, using self-constructed stock market indices for 2023-2025. By capturing both static dependence and dynamic patterns, we assess how intrasectoral relationships evolve over time and under varying market conditions. We detect strong positive relationships among the four AI industries, which intensify during periods of market stress. Cross-industry spillovers account for more than half of return variation in the AI sector, though they remain modest under normal conditions. During sharp market swings, particularly downturns, shocks propagate widely across all industries. While AI hardware manufacturers and AI BigTech typically act as net shock transmitters and AI application developers and cloud providers as net receivers, their roles shift over time. Our results emphasize the need for dynamic hedging, as static diversification offers limited protection in stressed markets, and closer monitoring of cross-industry exposures. Given the growing dependence of many sectors on AI infrastructure, disruptions in key AI segments may have wider systemic effects and should be incorporated into macroprudential oversight.

title: The Regional Integration Shock: A Quasi-Natural Experiment on the RCEP Agreement and Bank Efficiency
affiliations: , Universiti Malaya, University of Malaya and University of Malaya (UM) - Faculty of Business & Accountancy

detail.title: The Regional Integration Shock: A Quasi-Natural Experiment on the RCEP Agreement and Bank Efficiency
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of the Regional Integration on bank efficiency (BE) in the Asia-Pacific region. Using the implementation of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) as an exogenous policy shock, we construct a difference-in-differences model based on panel data from 304 commercial banks in both RCEP and non-RCEP economies between 2018 and 2024. The results show that RCEP framework significantly improves BE, and these findings remain robust across a series of checks. Mechanism analysis reveals that loan expansion and net interest margin are potential transmission channels through which RCEP enhances efficiency by promoting scale effects and reducing information asymmetry. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis indicates that this positive impact is significant only in countries with lower regulatory quality, weaker government effectiveness and poorer corruption control, suggesting a compensatory rather than an enhancement effect. This study provides the evidence that regional trade agreements can improve financial institutional performance and underscores the importance of regional cooperation in strengthening financial resilience.

title: An Agenda for Plastics Crisis Research
affiliations: University of Gothenburg, Lund University, University of Oregon, University of Washington and University of Gothenburg

detail.title: An Agenda for Plastics Crisis Research
detail.abstract: This survey synthesizes insights from environmental social sciences to recast the plastics crisis as a structural feature of growth‑dependent economies rather than a problem solvable by consumer choice or incremental technologies. Rather than a within‑field review of ecological economics, it maps adjacent literatures to specify what this field should study and how, clarifying researchable questions, suitable methods, and tractable indicators. The synthesis foregrounds connections between expansionary political‑economic dynamics, globally uneven socio‑ecological burdens across the plastics life cycle, and the power and knowledge relations that shape what is produced, measured, and governed. It calls for comparative, mixed‑methods, multi‑scalar work and for open, standardized data on plastics flows to strengthen causal inference and comparability. Shifting attention upstream—from end‑of‑pipe fixes to the transformation of provisioning systems—the paper charts lines of inquiry capable of aligning social metabolism with biophysical limits and human needs, providing a roadmap for ecological economics to organize and accelerate research beyond consumer or techno‑managerial framings.

title: On the prediction of peak overpressure using a physics-informed weighted neural network
affiliations: , Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing Institute of Technology, North University of China and

detail.title: On the prediction of peak overpressure using a physics-informed weighted neural network
detail.abstract: Accurate prediction of explosion shock wave parameters is crucial for explosion hazard assessment and blast-resistant structure design. Traditional simulation methods, such as computational fluid dynamics, can simulate the propagation process of explosion shock waves in complex environments, but they are difficult to meet the demand for rapid assessment. Existing neural network models have demonstrated high efficiency and accuracy in overpressure prediction, but the prediction range of these models is limited by the training domain, making it impossible to predict data outside the training domain. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a physics-informed weighted neural network framework (PIWNN) based on traditional physical models. This framework consists of a physical model layer and a weight coefficient layer. By training the weight parameters of multiple physical models, it addresses these limitations and the model has good generalization and extrapolation capabilities. The PIWNN model has an error rate of no more than 10% for predicting the proportion of distance beyond the training domain at 99.54%, and an error rate of no more than 10% for predicting the proportion of blast height beyond the training domain at 96.72%. Compared with existing neural network models, the prediction error of the PIWNN model is reduced by at least 28.3%. Compared with traditional physical models, the prediction error of the PIWNN model is reduced by at least 42.2%. Additionally, the PIWNN model requires only 170 hyperparameters to be trained, significantly reducing the model's complexity. The PIWNN model proposed in this study can provide important references for modeling regression problems in engineering design.

title: Tracing Wood Carbon from global Forests through the Processing Hub Austria
affiliations: Universität für Bodenkultur Wien (BOKU), , Universität für Bodenkultur Wien (BOKU), Vienna University of Economics and Business, Vienna University of Economics and Business, Universität für Bodenkultur Wien (BOKU) and Universität für Bodenkultur Wien (BOKU)

detail.title: Tracing Wood Carbon from global Forests through the Processing Hub Austria
detail.abstract: Conventional LULUCF accounting attributes forest carbon loss to the country where harvesting occurs, while setting emissions from wood processing to zero. Although globally consistent, this approach induces flawed policy incentives when assessing the impacts of wood processing. To address this, processing industries must be linked to forest carbon flows in origin countries. Focusing on Austria—a major wood processing hub— we integrate detailed national wood supply chain data with the global wood trade model FORBIO for the 2015–2017 average. By applying country-specific harvest loss factors, we estimate the gross harvest embodied in Austria’s wood flows and compare it to forest carbon dynamics in origin countries. Austria’s gross harvest was over four times its forest carbon sink. Gross harvest embodied in imports from major neighboring countries equaled to 15–170% of their own forest carbon sinks or sources. Of all processing industries, the sawmill and pulp-paper industries had the highest embodied gross harvest (6.7 and 4.6 Mt C/yr, respectively); Of the final uses, 7.1 Mt C/yr were embodied in energy use, 3.8 Mt C/yr in material use, and 6.0 Mt C/yr in exports. The input-based account of embodied gross harvest, i.e. gross harvest of domestic extraction plus imports, was 1.6 times the consumption-based footprint. While sawmills relied largely on European sources, the paper sector sourced 12% of its embodied harvest from Asia and the Americas. Our results relativize climate neutrality claims of wood processing and end uses, show the importance of input-based accounts for hub countries, and nuance regionality claims.

title: A discrete choice experiment to measure the impact of flood risk information on residential location choices
affiliations: University of Lorraine,  and

detail.title: A discrete choice experiment to measure the impact of flood risk information on residential location choices
detail.abstract: This article investigates residential choices in flood-prone areas with attractive natural amenities. A discrete choice experiment with 472 French homeowners examines the effects of flood risk information disclosure on residential choices. Respondents make trade-offs between house characteristics, amenities and flood-prone locations, with two information treatments on flood consequences and protection measures. We also assess the role of existing information tools. Econometric results show a general aversion to flood-prone areas, with flood consequence information having a negative effect. The knowledge of existing information tools reinforces this general aversion. However, on average, zoning has a positive effect on individuals’ decisions to stay, while knowledge of regulatory buyer-tenant information does not have this effect.

title: Pushing the Limit: How Borrowers Tackle an LTV Cap
affiliations: Ghent University - Department of Financial Economics, , Ghent University and

detail.title: Pushing the Limit: How Borrowers Tackle an LTV Cap
detail.abstract: We study how mortgage borrowers adjust their mortgage terms and household balance sheets in response to a loan-to-value (LTV) limit. Focusing on the 2020 Belgian LTV policy, we use granular loan- and account-level data from the country’s largest bank. A substantial share of borrowers reduced their LTV ratios, with adjustment patterns varying by income, liquid wealth, and household type. Borrowers mainly responded by increasing downpayments and reducing loan amounts, though these responses were weaker among lower-income households. While the adjustments led to safer mortgages, they were also associated with declines in liquid wealth and consumption in the year following purchase.

title: Synergistic Evolution of Resilience and Efficiency in China's Freshwater Aquaculture Systems under Water-Food-Carbon Constraints
affiliations: Shanghai Ocean University and Macquarie University

detail.title: Synergistic Evolution of Resilience and Efficiency in China's Freshwater Aquaculture Systems under Water-Food-Carbon Constraints
detail.abstract: Freshwater aquaculture is a major contributor to aquatic food supply, yet its sustainable development is increasingly constrained by growing competition for water resources, food security pressures, and carbon mitigation targets. These interacting pressures form a coupled water-food-carbon (WFC) constraint system that reshapes the stability and long-term development of freshwater aquaculture. While production efficiency and system resilience are both critical for sustainability, their dynamic interaction under compound constraints remains poorly understood.This study develops an integrated framework to quantify WFC constraint intensity, freshwater aquaculture resilience, and production efficiency, and to examine their synergistic evolution. Using provincial panel data from China for the period 2008-2023, a synergetics (Haken) model is applied to analyse the dynamic relationship between efficiency and resilience under WFC constraints. Random forest and SHAP analyses are further used to identify key drivers of system coordination and their nonlinear effects.The results indicate that water-related pressures dominate the constraints faced by freshwater aquaculture, with food and carbon pressures playing reinforcing roles. Under tightening WFC constraints, system dynamics shift from resilience-led to efficiency-led evolution, indicating that short-term efficiency increasingly governs system adjustment. At the national level, coordination between efficiency and resilience follows a rise-then-decline trajectory, reflecting a transitional phase in which efficiency gains are insufficient to sustain resilience. Spatially, central provinces exhibit relatively higher coordination, while eastern regions face intensified resource and environmental pressures and western and northeastern regions lag due to structural limitations. Environmental regulation, agricultural water use, economic development, vegetation conditions, and transport infrastructure are identified as key drivers, all showing pronounced nonlinear responses.Overall, the findings suggest that sustainable freshwater aquaculture requires coordinated strategies that jointly enhance efficiency and resilience under compound resource and carbon constraints.

title: Increasing conflict between intuitions triggers deliberation
affiliations: Cornell University and Cornell University

detail.title: Increasing conflict between intuitions triggers deliberation
detail.abstract: Despite decades of research on human reasoning, a deceptively simple question remains empirically underexplored: what makes us reason? Classical Dual Process Theories (DPTs) struggle with this question because they posit an intuitive System 1 whose outputs are monitored and sometimes overridden by a deliberative System 2. This creates a theoretical paradox: System 2 would need to both detect the need for additional processing and perform that processing, behaving like a system that triggers itself. In contrast, “hybrid” DPTs resolve the paradoxical tension by proposing that conflict between competing (System 1 generated) intuitions serves as the cue that triggers analytic engagement. Although this view has become dominant, little empirical work has attempted to manipulate the strength differential of competing intuitions to test the core prediction that, by doing so, deliberation should be triggered. We test this prediction by modifying the classic base-rate neglect paradigm in a within-participant experiment with six counterbalanced conditions (N=263). Our design extends the classic base-rate–versus–stereotype conflict by introducing a novel source of conflict: within-stereotype conflict. We systematically vary whether the stereotypical descriptions by themselves evoke one or two competing intuitions—and manipulate whether the base-rate supports one or another stereotype-derived intuition. Increasing conflict between intuitions in this manner led to probability judgments that “neglect” the base-rate less, are less confident, and (suggesting increased deliberation) take more time to be generated. Thus, our results provide empirical support for hybrid DPTs.

title: Incorporating Regret Aversion into Emerging Market Portfolios
affiliations: University of Novi Sad

detail.title: Incorporating Regret Aversion into Emerging Market Portfolios

contentType.other: Final accepted version. Forthcoming in Spanish Journal of Finance and Accounting (REFC).

detail.abstract: This paper examines how incorporating regret aversion affects portfolio construction and performance in emerging stock markets. Using daily data from 2015-2025, the paper builds multivariate six-asset portfolios for Central and Eastern Europe (CEEC), East Asia, and Latin America, alongside a G7 benchmark. A regret-minimizing portfolio is compared with traditional minimum-variance and maximum-Sharpe portfolios across pre-crisis and crisis periods. Results show that regret-averse portfolios are more diversified and place greater emphasis on low correlation assets, reducing the likelihood of extreme underperformance relative to the bestperforming asset. Emerging markets exhibit higher regret than developed markets, with the Latin American portfolios showing the largest regret levels. Notably, the CEEC portfolio consistently demonstrates the strongest performance, delivering the lowest regret and favourable risk-return outcomes in both subsamples. Robustness checks, including bootstrapping, variance-equality tests, and varying regret preferences, confirm the stability of the regret-minimizing approach and highlight its practical relevance for behaviourally sensitive investors.

title: Green Investments and Worker Voice
affiliations: Università di Parma, University of Parma - Dipartimento di Scienze Economiche e Aziendali and University of Parma

detail.title: Green Investments and Worker Voice
detail.abstract: The interaction between organised employee representation (ER) and firms' engagement in the green transition remains insufficiently understood. Theoretically, two opposing mechanisms may operate. In the bargaining view, representation can slow green investments by increasing adjustment costs and exposing firms to rent-seeking pressures. In contrast, the employee voice perspective holds that ER enables sustainability by facilitating information exchange, eliciting workers' environmental preferences, and supporting joint problem-solving when organisational adaptation is required. We test these predictions using survey and administrative data from nearly 2,000 firms in Emilia-Romagna. Firms with ER are systematically more likely to pursue green investments, especially in climate mitigation, water use, circularity, and pollution prevention. These results also hold when accounting for the endogeneity of ER via IV. Consistent with the voice mechanism, the association between ER and green investments is stronger in firms employing younger and more educated workers, who are more likely to hold proenvironmental preferences and contribute specialised knowledge relevant for organisational change. Taken together, our findings challenge the view that organised labour inhibits the green transition. Instead, ER emerges as a strategic policy lever that can foster decarbonisation pathways that are technologically feasible, socially negotiated, and democratically anchored at the workplace level.

title: Coase's Fable
affiliations: Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico

detail.title: Coase's Fable
detail.abstract: This paper is an updated version of my 2023 law review article "Coase's Parable." Here, I describe Ronald Coase's insight that harms are a reciprocal problem as "Coase's axiom" and investigate its origins in the history of ideas. Specifically, how did Coase come up with this counter-intuitive axiom? My conjecture is that he either borrowed or stole it from Arnold Plant or had an "aha" moment sometime after reading a series of nuisance law cases in one of Plant's undergraduate courses.
