title: Playing it Safe or Playing Favorites? Miller Act Bonds and the Cost of Exclusion of Women- and Minority-Owned Businesses.
affiliations: Pace University - Elisabeth Haub School of Law

detail.title: Playing it Safe or Playing Favorites? Miller Act Bonds and the Cost of Exclusion of Women- and Minority-Owned Businesses.
detail.abstract:
As federal contracting policy has moved away from race- and gender-conscious contracting initiatives, the need to identify and remove facially neutral requirements that create disparate impacts has assumed heightened significance in shaping access to government contracting law. In construction projects, the federal government has long required contractors to purchase surety bonds under the Miller Act to protect subcontractors and the government in cases of prime contractor default. While that original purpose remains valid today, bonding requirements are widely believed to unnecessarily limit participation by women- and minority-owned businesses. 

            Federal, state, and local governments have tacitly accepted the claim that bonding requirements create barriers to entry for women- and minority-owned businesses, with many programs aimed at promoting broader participation by relaxing these requirements. Despite decades of debate, both proponents and opponents have offered little empirical evidence to support their positions. At the same time, government officials increasingly justify bonding requirements as financial safeguards, but also as a secondary vetting mechanism for contractor reliability. 

            This article argues that while bonding remains necessary for larger projects, the federal government should reconsider their use on smaller projects for two reasons. First, the government’s current implicit cost-benefit analysis for requiring surety bonds is inherently incomplete, as it fails to account for indirect costs such as the exclusion of Women- and Minority-owned businesses. To support this claim, I present the first empirical evidence that bonding requirements function as a barrier to entry for these firms. Second, the government’s reliance on sureties as a vetting mechanism improperly duplicates the functions of contracting officers, who are already tasked with ensuring that only “responsible” contractors receive government contracts. This dual-vetting system is generating costs and accountability gaps in federal procurement. If the government chooses to retain sureties in this capacity, then procurement regulations should reflect that delegation; otherwise, the contracting officer should retake full ownership and accountability for this function. 

Finally, I propose a conceptual framework that accounts for both the direct and indirect effects of bonding requirements while respecting established government contracting principles. Drawing on the costs and benefits of surety bonds and procurement law, I explore several policy alternatives that can help reconcile the government’s legitimate risk mitigation interest with statutory mandates to promote broad contractor participation in federal markets.

title: Social Movement and Gender Disparities in Promotions: Evidence from the #MeToo Movement
affiliations: Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University, Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University and Colorado State University, Fort Collins - Department of Finance & Real Estate

detail.title: Social Movement and Gender Disparities in Promotions: Evidence from the #MeToo Movement
detail.abstract: We document that the #MeToo movement significantly narrows the gender promotion gap within firms by advancing female managers’ careers relative to male colleagues. The effect is stronger for lower-ranking and younger managers and is not driven by tokenism. At the firm level, the promotion gap declines after #MeToo, particularly in firms with stronger pre-existing sexist cultures. This greater decline in sexist firms is primarily driven by institutional investor pressure and is weaker in Republican-leaning states and states with restrictive labor mobility. Firm value rises following the narrowing of gender disparities, despite stagnant operating performance and a decline in productivity. Mobility patterns show that #MeToo changes labor-market sorting: female managers are less likely to leave and more likely to join sexist firms, whereas male managers are more likely to leave but not join such firms. Overall, the movement plays a corrective role in reducing gender disparities and reshaping managerial labor-market dynamics.

title: The Color of Knowledge: Impacts of Tutor Race on Learning and Performance
affiliations: University of Milan, Johannes Kepler University Linz and University of Erlangen-Nuremberg-Friedrich Alexander Universität Erlangen Nürnberg

detail.title: The Color of Knowledge: Impacts of Tutor Race on Learning and Performance
detail.abstract: We demonstrate that racial biases against tutors hinder learning. In e-learning experiments, U.S. conservatives are more likely to disregard advice from Black tutors, resulting in reduced performance compared to learners taught by white tutors. We show that the bias is unconscious and, consequently, does not skew tutor selection. In line with our theory, the bias disappears when the stakes are high. In contrast, liberals favor Black tutors without experiencing learning disparities. Methodologically, we contribute by using video post-production techniques to manipulate tutor race without introducing typical confounds. Additionally, we develop a novel two-stage design that simultaneously measures tutor selection, learning, and productivity.

title: Indigenous Mediation and Continental Integration: Lessons from Ghana for AfCFTA Dispute Resolution Framework
affiliations: The Chartered Institute of Arbitrators

detail.title: Indigenous Mediation and Continental Integration: Lessons from Ghana for AfCFTA Dispute Resolution Framework
detail.abstract: This article examines the role of indigenous mediation in advancing Africa’s continental integration agenda, using the recent mediation led by His Majesty Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, Asantehene of Ghana, in the Bawku chieftaincy dispute as a case study. The mediation process, formally mandated in 2025 and conducted within a constitutional framework, demonstrates how traditional authority can be effectively aligned with modern governance structures to resolve complex and protracted conflicts. The article argues that mediation is not foreign to African legal systems but is deeply rooted in communal doctrines that prioritize consensus, relationship preservation, and social cohesion over adversarial outcomes. Drawing lessons from the Ghanaian experience, the article evaluates the strategic relevance of mediation for the African Continental Free Trade Area, particularly in addressing cross-border disputes that intersect with customary practices, informal trade networks, and diverse legal traditions. It concludes that institutionalizing mediation as a core component of the AfCFTA dispute resolution mechanism would enhance legitimacy, compliance, and sustainability, while leveraging Africa’s indigenous dispute resolution heritage to support long-term economic integration.

title: Financial Mathematics Exact Equivalences and Structure-Preserving Correspondences
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: Financial Mathematics Exact Equivalences and Structure-Preserving Correspondences
detail.abstract: We present a comprehensive taxonomy of thirty-four mathematical correspondences connecting financial mathematics with statistical physics, quantum mechanics, differential geometry, optimal transport theory, and abstract algebra. Rather than claiming universal "isomorphism," we carefully classify each correspondence into one of five types: (A) exact isomorphisms with explicit invertible maps, (B) equivalences of formulation where distinct representations describe the same mathematical object, (C) duality relationships arising from optimization or variational principles, (D) limit theorems and weak convergence results, and (E) shared algebraic structures providing computational or conceptual parallels. For each correspondence, we specify the underlying mathematical objects, function spaces, regularity conditions, and the precise sense in which structure is preserved. This classification enables rigorous transfer of techniques across domains while avoiding the pitfalls of false analogy. The framework has practical implications for derivatives pricing, portfolio optimization, risk management, and machine learning in finance.

title: Transforming Strategy with AI and Cloud: A Case Study of Dynamic Capabilities in Action at a Fortune 500 Firm
affiliations: University of Girona, Students and University of Girona

detail.title: Transforming Strategy with AI and Cloud: A Case Study of Dynamic Capabilities in Action at a Fortune 500 Firm
detail.abstract: How do large, legacy-rich firms reconfigure their strategic orientation amid rapid technological change? This study investigates how a Fortune 500 company developed dynamic capabilities to drive enterprise-wide transformation through AI and cloud integration. Drawing on the Dynamic Capabilities Framework, we analyze 22 interviews and multiple data sources to trace how sensing, seizing, and transforming capabilities were orchestrated across internal structures and external ecosystems. Transformation emerged as a continuous, evolving process involving structural redesign, workforce reskilling, partner engagement, and leadership-driven cultural adaptation. The study contributes to dynamic capabilities theory by revealing how capability orchestration extends beyond internal routines, involving ecosystem collaboration, strategic acquisitions, and AI-enabled learning to build adaptive capacity. These findings offer an empirically grounded process model of how digital technologies drive strategic renewal in complex, resource-heavy environments, advancing our understanding of the microfoundations of dynamic capabilities and offering insights for managing digital transformation in traditional industries.

title: Zero-Shot LLM Agents for Explainable Bridge Portfolio Maintenance Scheduling Under Uncertainty
affiliations: University of Naples, University of Naples and Department of Structural Engineering

detail.title: Zero-Shot LLM Agents for Explainable Bridge Portfolio Maintenance Scheduling Under Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Bridge maintenance scheduling requires decision-making under stochastic deterioration, epistemic uncertainty, and financial constraints. This work introduces a zero-shot Large Language Model (LLM)-based agent for maintenance scheduling in bridge networks, embedded within a physics-informed simulation environment that models non-linear degradation and budget dynamics. The agent operates solely through structured prompts specifying system state, feasible actions, and operational rules, and outputs explainable decisions together with a machine-readable action plan.The experimental campaign evaluates: (i) prompt configuration and memory mechanisms, (ii) five risk-aversion profiles, (iii) scalability with respect to the size of the bridge portfolio, and (iv) long-horizon behavior. The best agent configuration achieves stable performance with no structural failures and the highest financial efficiency. Prudent agents maintain consistently high structural reliability, whereas aggressive profiles exhibit reduced reliability and occasional failures, reflecting coherent behavioral differentiation. The finding of this work indicate that zero-shot LLM agents hold promise as explainable and adaptable decision-making components for infrastructure life-cycle management. The results suggest that LLM-driven strategies may complement, and potentially enhance, existing scheduling and rule-based maintenance frameworks, motivating further investigation into real-world deployments and integration with domain-specific models.

title: Sustainability Strategies and Firm Value
affiliations: Imperial College Business School

detail.title: Sustainability Strategies and Firm Value
detail.abstract: Despite the diffusion of sustainability as a legitimate strategic logic, scholarly evidence of its impact on firm value remains tentative. The prevailing emphasis on a "local business case", which focuses on proximate mechanisms, provides limited strategic guidance on how firms should adapt their behavior as systemic boundaries become more salient. This paper bridges this gap by developing a framework, grounded in complexity theory, that links the value of sustainability strategies to their ability to manage a multi-level feedback loop between firm operations and systemic outcomes. We posit that firms must develop strategic complexity, the degree of sophistication of their strategies in terms of the breadth of implied sustainability behaviors, to match the systemic complexity of the environment they are embedded in. Due to cognitive and organizational costs, this relationship is not linear but follows an inverted U-shape. Furthermore, we hypothesize that this curve shifts when exogenous shocks alter systemic complexity. To test these predictions, we develop a novel methodology, applying a hierarchical Bayesian model to a dataset of over 200,000 corporate sustainability initiatives by 1,186 firms to measure the complexity of their enacted strategies. Our empirical design leverages the European Union's "Fit for 55" policy as a quasi-natural experiment in a continuous treatment, triple difference-indifferences framework. Our results support both hypotheses: we find a curvilinear relationship between strategic complexity and firm financial value, and show that the curve shifts toward higher complexity for EU firms following the regulatory shock.

title: Subcontracting Networks, Competition and Firm Participation in Public Procurement1
affiliations: University of Oklahoma - Department of Economics, Moravian College, Google LLC and Oklahoma City Community College

detail.title: Subcontracting Networks, Competition and Firm Participation in Public Procurement1
detail.abstract: We study how network structures in road construction shape subcontracting opportunities and market outcomes using Bayesian methods. We find that, the likelihood of forming new contractual relationships decreases when prime contractors have extensive networks, but increases when subcontractors are connected to key industry players. Subcontracting imposes non-linear bid premiums that shrink with project size, subcontracting share, or subcontractor count, creating cost advantages for large contracts. Controlling for project characteristics, well-connected primes raise winning bids, and network ties reduce firms’ exit risk, underscoring the strategic value of connections.

title: Selecting Non-Recurrent Upstream Partners for R&D Collaborations: The Effect of Social Heuristics
affiliations: University of York and Keio University

detail.title: Selecting Non-Recurrent Upstream Partners for R&D Collaborations: The Effect of Social Heuristics

keywords: Heuristics Based on Recency and Status

detail.abstract: This study examines how multinational enterprises (MNE) select upstream partners for R&D collaborations. Non-recurrent partners with limited prior alliance history can help the focal firm reconfigure network strategy. However, relatively little is known about how MNEs recognize and select non-recurrent partners, despite alliance inertia favoring recurrent partners. In this research, we tested whether recent positive news, such as a positive sales surprise, can increase the likelihood that the focal MNE forms an R&D alliance with non-recurrent partners, given the market’s tendency to recognize a firm’s strategy based on positive recent news. Non-recurrent partners are categorized into three sub-groups: new, nascent, and dormant. A series of tests based on dyads of alliances in the automotive sector found that recent news positively influences the focal MNE’s propensity to form R&D alliances with partners, and that non-recurrent partners remain secondary options. However, further analysis showed that a nascent partner, a specific sub-group, can increase its likelihood of collaborating with the focal firm, given both recent news and its status confirmed in the industry. We conceptualize recent news and status as evidence of social heuristics that can mitigate the influence of alliance inertia on repeated partner selection decisions. Further tests were conducted using the treatment-effect model to address endogeneity bias and a difference-in-differences analysis to identify the salience of social heuristics changing over time with volatile environments.

title: Model predictive control for air to water heat pump in context of explicit flexibility: from design to hardware in the loop experiment
affiliations: Mines Paris - PSL, Mines Paris - PSL, Mines Paris - PSL, ,  and

detail.title: Model predictive control for air to water heat pump in context of explicit flexibility: from design to hardware in the loop experiment
detail.abstract: Building electrification through heat pumps and renewable energies deployment have pushed for a growing interest in leveraging building flexibility to support the grid. To do so, advanced control strategies for heat pumps specifically designed to address flexibility are required. In that context, this study presents the development of a flexibility-focused controller for heat pumps to meet explicit demand response schemes especially relying on shutdown orders. The primary objective is to enhance the response of Heat Pumps (HP) to the grid orders while maintaining safe and efficient HP operations and suitable user comfort. To achieve this goal, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework is developed and combined with additional expert Rule-Based Control (RBC) rules. The controller is then tested on a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test bench. The tests demonstrate significant improvements in energy management by reducing consumption by 16% as well as reducing discomfort degree-hours by 75% compared to baseline control over the course of 4 winter days. Finally, this study highlights that in order not to degrade HP performance after a shutdown order, it is preferable to maintain standby electricity consumption for immediate compressor availability. This enables a significant mitigation of rebound effects after the shutdown period.

title: Ideology in Action: Influence of Political Ideological Imprints on Corporate Green Innovation in China
affiliations: , Renmin University of China,  and

detail.title: Ideology in Action: Influence of Political Ideological Imprints on Corporate Green Innovation in China
detail.abstract: Despite the growing body of research linking political ideology and organizational ethical practices, limited studies have examined whether and how political ideological imprints affect green innovation in China’s unique market-oriented socialist system. We examine the impact of directors’ communist ideological imprints on corporate green innovation. Using a sample of 13,343 firm–year observations for Chinese non-state-owned listed firms from 2006 to 2021, we demonstrate a positive correlation between communist ideological imprints and green innovation. Notably, we find that green innovation spillover effects occur within these independent directors’ social networks. We also reveal that regional political values and patriotic culture strengthen directors’ ideological imprints. The positive impact of political ideological imprints on green innovation and its spillovers is amplified when independent directors possess heightened reputation incentives and power, and when firms encounter stringent environment regulations. Our findings extend the research on political ideology and the imprinting theory, highlighting the role of political ideology in encouraging green innovation in the emerging Chinese market.

title: Improving dependability in robotized bolting operations
affiliations: , , , Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and

detail.title: Improving dependability in robotized bolting operations
detail.abstract: Bolting operations are critical in industrial assembly and in the maintenance of scientific facilities, requiring high precision and robustness to faults. Although robotic solutions have the potential to improve operational safety and effectiveness, current systems still lack reliable autonomy and fault management capabilities. To address this gap, we propose a control framework for dependable robotized bolting tasks and instantiate it on a specific robotic system. The system features a control architecture ensuring accurate driving torque control and active compliance throughout the entire operation, enabling safe interaction even under fault conditions.By designing a multimodal human-robot interface (HRI) providing real-time visualization of relevant system information and supporting seamless transitions between automatic and manual control, we improve operator situation awareness and fault detection capabilities. A high-level supervisor (SV) coordinates the execution and manages transitions between control modes, ensuring consistency with the supervisory control (SVC) paradigm, while preserving the human operator's authority.The system is validated in a representative bolting operation involving pipe flange joining, under several fault conditions.The results demonstrate improved fault detection capabilities, enhanced operator situational awareness, and accurate and compliant execution of the bolting operation. However, they also reveal the limitations of relying on a single camera to achieve full situational awareness.

title: Sustainable port maintenance: dredging equipment selection in time-emission trade-offs
affiliations: , , ,  and Delft University of Technology

detail.title: Sustainable port maintenance: dredging equipment selection in time-emission trade-offs
detail.abstract: Maintenance dredging in ports and waterways is essential to ensure safe navigation. With increasing regulatory pressure on the maritime sector to reduce exhaust emissions, both dredging contractors and port authorities are seeking effective mitigation strategies. However, accurate emission estimates for maintenance dredging activities are still limited in the literature and often rely on experiential knowledge rather than scientific methodologies. This study suggests a method for estimating emissions and comparing alternative maintenance dredging strategies by quantifying trade-offs between project duration, energy consumption, and emissions. The method integrates vessel characteristics, project specifications, and sediment properties to allow for situation-specific, realistic assessments. A discrete-event simulation is used to evaluate two alternative scenarios, offering insights into the impact of key parameters on vessel selection and overall operational efficiency. The method is demonstrated using a case study of the Port of Ramsgate (UK), where estimated results are compared with real-world data for validation. Finally, the study outlines theoretical and managerial implications and suggests directions for future research.

title: Resolving Fuel Supply Inertia in Coal-Fired Boilers Using Small Pulverized Coal Silo: Dynamic Simulation for Enhanced Operational Flexibility
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology - State Key Laboratory of Coal Combustion, Huazhong University of Science and Technology - State Key Laboratory of Coal Combustion, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology - State Key Laboratory of Coal Combustion, Huazhong University of Science and Technology - State Key Laboratory of Coal Combustion, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology - State Key Laboratory of Coal Combustion and Huazhong University of Science and Technology - State Key Laboratory of Coal Combustion

detail.title: Resolving Fuel Supply Inertia in Coal-Fired Boilers Using Small Pulverized Coal Silo: Dynamic Simulation for Enhanced Operational Flexibility
detail.abstract: The global energy transition necessitates a higher share of renewable energy sources, requiring coal-fired power plants (CFPPs) to provide flexible operation to compensate for renewable volatility. However, conventional CFPPs are constrained by fuel supply inertia, hindering their ability to meet dynamic grid demands. This paper proposes coupling a Small Pulverized Coal Silo (SPCS) system between the pulverizing system and the boiler to provide rapid fuel feeding. A high-fidelity dynamic simulation model of a 350 MW boiler integrated with the SPCS was developed, and the boiler subsystem was rigorously validated against plant data. Results demonstrate that the SPCS system significantly enhances the boiler load change rate, with the average ramp rate increasing from 1.26%Pe/min to 3.23%Pe/min when supplying 7 kg/s of coal during the 50%-75% load range. Moreover, this enhancement was more pronounced in the lower load range compared to the higher load range (75%-100%). To mitigate resulting main steam temperature fluctuations, a dynamic feedwater compensation strategy was implemented. An optimal compensation water-to-fuel ratio of 5, translating to a maximum compensation water flow of 25 kg/s, was identified, maintaining main steam temperature within 550–580 °C. Furthermore, initiating feedwater compensation 100s in advance proved superior to synchronous strategies, effectively suppressing overshoots. This study demonstrates that the SPCS system provides a viable solution for enhancing flexibility and offers operational guidance for coordinated fuel and water regulation.

title: Data-Driven NMPC of Grading Operations for Excavators: Approaches and Experimental Results
affiliations: Polytechnic University of Milan, Polytechnic University of Milan, Robert Bosch GmbH and Polytechnic University of Milan

detail.title: Data-Driven NMPC of Grading Operations for Excavators: Approaches and Experimental Results

keywords: Trajectory tracking and path following for AVs

detail.abstract: Hydraulic excavators are crucial for tasks like levelling and creating sloped surfaces, requiring high precision. Automation can boost productivity by improving accuracy and reducing reliance on skilled labour. However, the non-linearities and variability in hydraulic systems make controller design challenging. Two data-driven Model Predictive Control (MPC) approaches are presented, ideal for handling non-linear dynamics and system constraints: the first with a trajectory tracking formulation and the second with a path following one. The system model is based on Linear Local Models averaged by non-linear membership functions, trained with the LOcal LInear MOdel Tree (LOLIMOT) algorithm, an approach that is simple to linearize for efficient online implementation of the MPC laws.The data-driven nature of the model ensures flexibility and the ability to handle diverse real-world scenarios. The control system was tested on a full-scale JCB Hydradig 110W, the results demonstrate that the MPC approaches significantly outperform previous data-based controllers. Moreover, a comparison between the two MPC formulations indicates that path following outperforms trajectory tracking in this specific application.

title: Extending the application of dynamic Bayesian networks in calculating market risk: Standard and stressed expected shortfall
affiliations: , University of Cape Town and University of Cape Town

detail.title: Extending the application of dynamic Bayesian networks in calculating market risk: Standard and stressed expected shortfall
detail.abstract: In the last five years, expected shortfall (ES) and stressed ES (SES) have become key required regulatory measures of market risk in the banking sector, especially following events such as the global financial crisis. Thus, finding ways to optimize their estimation is of great importance. We extend the application of dynamic Bayesian networks (DBNs) to the estimation of 10-day 97.5% ES and stressed ES, building on prior work applying DBNs to value at risk. Using the S&P 500 index as a proxy for the equities trading desk of a US bank, we compare the performance of three DBN structure-learning algorithms with several traditional market risk models, using either the normal or the skewed Student’s t return distributions. Backtesting shows that all models fail to produce statistically accurate ES and SES forecasts at the 2.5% level, reflecting the difficulty of modeling extreme tail behavior. For ES, the EGARCH(1,1) model (normal) produces the most accurate forecasts, while, for SES, the GARCH(1,1) model (normal) performs best. All distribution-dependent models deteriorate substantially when using the skewed Student’s t distribution. The DBNs perform comparably to the historical simulation model, but their contribution to tail prediction is limited by the small weight assigned to their one-day-ahead forecasts within the return distribution. Future research should examine weighting schemes that enhance the influence of forward-looking DBN forecasts on tail risk estimation.

title: Unlocking Team Productivity in Hierarchical Cultures: How Psychological Safety Turns Individual Strengths into Collective Results
affiliations: and

detail.title: Unlocking Team Productivity in Hierarchical Cultures: How Psychological Safety Turns Individual Strengths into Collective Results
detail.abstract: In hierarchical cultures where deference to authority is paramount, team productivity is frequently constrained not by a lack of individual talent but by a climate of silence where employees withhold insights due to perceived risk. This study addresses a critical gap in the literature by examining whether psychological safety—a team climate for interpersonal risk-taking—can be cultivated and drive performance in high power-distance contexts. Leveraging a rigorous, six-month longitudinal field study of 420 employees and 86 supervisors in Iran’s service sector, we demonstrate that psychological safety is not a Western luxury but a universal performance lever. It acts as the essential bridge that unlocks latent individual strengths, translating them into collective outcomes. Our findings reveal that teams with high psychological safety outperform their low-safety counterparts by up to 30% in productivity, while simultaneously strengthening trust in leadership by 41%. Critically, safety is shown to reinforce—not erode—hierarchical respect by reframing constructive voice as a duty to collective success. We translate these insights into a manager-ready, culturally intelligent playbook, providing a three-pillar framework, diagnostic checklist, and a phased 30–60–90-day action plan to build safety without destabilizing cultural norms.

title: Low-Resolution Perception for Robotic Packing
affiliations: Polytechnic University of Milan, Polytechnic University of Milan, Polytechnic University of Milan, Polytechnic University of Milan, Polytechnic University of Milan and Polytechnic University of Milan

detail.title: Low-Resolution Perception for Robotic Packing

keywords: Smart production and logistics in manufacturing

detail.abstract: This work tackles the problem of scalable perception for robotic packing with lowcost, low-resolution depth sensing. We propose a framework where reconstruction cues drive next-view selection and grasp evidence updates a per-object stability estimate, jointly deciding what to acquire next and when to grasp. During the reconstruction, a low-resolution Next Best View (NBV) strategy explicitly avoids redundant views while preserving task-relevant geometry. We validate the approach in two steps: (i) an ablation study of the utility function under very low resolution, and (ii) a full end-to-end evaluation across policies, showing how low-resolution perception is a practical, scalable option for robotic packing.

title: Toward ESG-driven sustainable transition in third-party logistics: Addressing obstacles and mitigation strategies through QFD under interval-valued spherical fuzzy model
affiliations: Mahidol University and Mahidol University

detail.title: Toward ESG-driven sustainable transition in third-party logistics: Addressing obstacles and mitigation strategies through QFD under interval-valued spherical fuzzy model
detail.abstract: Although the importance of ESG practices in logistics is widely recognized, small and medium-sized third-party logistics providers (SME 3PLs) continue to face significant barriers that hinder sustainable transition. The most pressing challenges include weak collaboration among supply chain actors, limited financial capacity, and fragmented regulatory frameworks. While prior studies have explored these issues conceptually, few have systematically assessed their relative influence or linked them to targeted mitigation strategies through structured decision approaches. To address this gap, the present study develops an integrated framework combining the Content Validity Ratio (CVR), Full Consistency Method (FUCOM), Decision Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), and Quality Function Deployment (QFD) under interval-valued spherical fuzzy (IVSF) modeling. The results highlight fragmented collaboration, capital shortages, and regulatory misalignment as the most critical barriers. In response, strategies such as strengthening collaboration with green suppliers and clients, fostering industry-level partnerships, and promoting leadership for sustainability transformation emerge as the most effective solutions. The study advances institutional theory by emphasizing the role of inter-organizational collaboration, extends the resource-based view (RBV) by demonstrating how financial resources function as strategic enablers, and applies the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework to capture the multidimensional drivers of ESG adoption. From a practical perspective, the findings guide managers and policymakers toward the design of collaborative platforms, innovative financing mechanisms, and coherent regulatory standards. Collectively, these insights provide a structured pathway for accelerating ESG-driven sustainability in logistics networks.

title: Deep Learning-Based Anomaly Detection in Electric Motors Production Using Mel-Spectrograms Representations and Hybrid Neural Network
affiliations: Jozef Stefan International Postgraduate School, Jožef Stefan Institute and Jožef Stefan Institute

detail.title: Deep Learning-Based Anomaly Detection in Electric Motors Production Using Mel-Spectrograms Representations and Hybrid Neural Network
detail.abstract: This paper presents a novel deep learning framework for detecting anomalies in motor acoustic and vibration signals, designed for End-of-Line (EoL) quality inspection in manufacturing. The proposed method leverages Mel-frequency spectrograms (MFSs) as input features and employs a hybrid neural network architecture that combines convolutional neural network (CNN) and bidirectional gated recurrent units (BiGRUs). This combination effectively captures both local spectral patterns and temporal dependencies, enabling robust differentiation between normal and abnormal motor behavior. Acoustic and vibrational data were collected from over 2400 motors during production, including approximately 2300 motors representing a reference dataset of healthy motor signals and smaller subset of approximately 100 motors representing faulty motors that provide anomaly instances. Experimental results on a separate subset of faulty motors demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high discrimination capability, with clear separation between healthy and faulty condition. Importantly, the method operates unsupervised and require no explicit fault labeling. This makes it highly suitable for scalable and automated EoL quality control in industrial manufacturing settings.

title: Downsizing in the age of artificial intelligence A dynamic multi-stakeholder framework of downsizing
affiliations: University of South Carolina, , Department of Communication Disorders Sciences and University of Connecticut - Department of Management

detail.title: Downsizing in the age of artificial intelligence A dynamic multi-stakeholder framework of downsizing
detail.abstract: Downsizing—the planned elimination of positions or jobs—amplifies organizational uncertainty and simultaneously affects employees, shareholders, customers, suppliers, and society, and is increasingly due to the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). Decades of downsizing research yield inconsistent conclusions because most studies focus on a single stakeholder group, failing to capture the complexity of effects on multiple stakeholder groups that are inherently affected by downsizing. An integrative framework that simultaneously examines the relationships and outcomes of different stakeholder groups affected by downsizing at different time periods, is needed to create a holistic understanding of the true impact of downsizing. Consequently, we conduct a review of downsizing organized by different stakeholder groups, synthesizing the literature from 2010 to 2025, and then develop a framework that integrates stakeholder theory and time horizon research, highlighting the rise in downsizing associated with the widespread adoption of AI. The proposed multi-stakeholder framework of downsizing incorporates how organizations identify, include, and prioritize different stakeholder groups during downsizing, and how behaviors and outcomes differ over time for different stakeholder groups. Our framework shifts the conversation in the downsizing literature from a debate of whether downsizing should occur to examining how downsizing may simultaneously yield positive and negative consequences for different stakeholders across short- and long-term time horizons.

title: High-precision IAS signal acquisition based on incremental encoder error self-compensation
affiliations: Kunming University of Science and Technology, Kunming University of Science and Technology, Kunming University of Science and Technology and Kunming University of Science and Technology

detail.title: High-precision IAS signal acquisition based on incremental encoder error self-compensation
detail.abstract: Instantaneous angular speed (IAS) signals are employed for servo motor control and rotating machinery fault diagnosis. However, manufacturing and installation processes of incremental optical encoders inevitably introduce encoder errors such as engraving, subdivision, and eccentricity errors, which degrade angle measurement accuracy and introduce noise in speed estimation. Therefore, this paper proposes a self-compensation method for the encoders under non-stationary operating conditions (SCM-NSOC), which enables online self-compensation of the encoders without disassembly or reliance on external calibration instruments. The proposed method overcomes the limitation of conventional constant elapsed time (CET) methods that require operation under steady-speed operating conditions. Based on the encoder error model, this study analyzes the mapping relationship between encoder errors and IAS signals, develops the SCM-NSOC, and extends the method to encoders that do not follow the error model. Experiments and simulations demonstrate that the proposed SCM-NSOC method effectively overcomes the limitations of the CET, achieving high-precision IAS signal acquisition.

title: Optimizing Agricultural Logistics: A Data-Driven P-Median Model for Palm Kernel Collection Center Locations in Tamil Nadu, India
affiliations: Rajalakshmi Engineering College - Department of Mechanical Engineering

detail.title: Optimizing Agricultural Logistics: A Data-Driven P-Median Model for Palm Kernel Collection Center Locations in Tamil Nadu, India
detail.abstract: This study develops and applies a data-driven facility location framework to identify optimal palm kernel collection center locations in Tamil Nadu, India. Using a P-median model, the analysis integrates taluk-level yield data, a distance matrix constructed from inter-taluk road distances, and transportation cost parameters across 54 taluks. The optimization identifies five collection centers that minimize total weighted travel distance while maintaining coverage of major production areas. The resulting locations—Rameshwaram, Uthangarai, Rasipuram, Krishnarayapuram, and Panruti—are validated using SITATION, a widely adopted facility location software, which produces identical assignments. A sensitivity analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of variations in yield and transport cost on total logistics costs, confirming that the recommended locations remain robust under moderate parameter changes. The study demonstrates how classical location-allocation models can be combined with regional agricultural data to support evidence-based infrastructure planning. The proposed approach provides a transparent decision-support tool for policymakers and agribusiness stakeholders seeking to reduce logistics burdens, improve farmer access to collection infrastructure, and promote the long-term sustainability of palm kernel supply chains.

title: Data as the New Stethoscope: How Big Data Analytics Is Reshaping Public Health Surveillance, Decision-Making, and Equity
affiliations: Cracow University of Economics and Nnamdi Azikiwe University

detail.title: Data as the New Stethoscope: How Big Data Analytics Is Reshaping Public Health Surveillance, Decision-Making, and Equity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: The integration of big data analytics into public health marks not merely a technological upgrade, but a foundational shift in how societies detect disease, respond to emergencies, design interventions, and pursue health equity. Drawing on evidence from 68 peer-reviewed studies (2017–2025), this narrative review synthesises advances and enduring challenges in applying big data analytics to public health decision-making. The analysis confirms transformative gains: AI-driven surveillance systems now detect outbreaks an average of 6–11 days earlier than traditional methods (Yang et al., 2023); real-time analytics have improved chronic disease risk stratification with AUCs exceeding 0.85 in high-quality validation studies (Chen et al., 2021); and decision support systems are increasingly embedded in national policy workflows—from pandemic response in South Korea to maternal health monitoring in Kenya (Moon et al., 2022; Oluoch et al., 2023). Yet, these advances coexist with serious constraints: inconsistent data governance, algorithmic bias against marginalised groups (Obermeyer et al., 2019), infrastructural gaps in low-resource settings, and a persistent evidence gap regarding long-term population health outcomes. Critically, the literature reveals that technical sophistication alone is insufficient; successful implementation hinges on institutional readiness, cross-sectoral collaboration, and ethical guardrails. This article argues that the future of public health lies not in more data, but in smarter stewardship—integrating analytics with equity-centred governance, workforce development, and community trust. We conclude with a pragmatic roadmap for researchers and policymakers, prioritising replicable frameworks over technical novelty.

title: Drive Smarter Quant Strategies Through the Implementation of Deep Learning (Presentation Slides)
affiliations: University of Reading

detail.title: Drive Smarter Quant Strategies Through the Implementation of Deep Learning (Presentation Slides)
detail.abstract:
This presentation studies the role of prediction, learning structure, and causality in quantitative portfolio construction. We first show that portfolio efficiency does not rely on accurate or causal forecasts of individual asset returns. Instead, efficiency is governed by three properties of predictive signals: directional alignment with true returns, correct cross-sectional ranking, and reasonable calibration. Under these conditions, even strongly misspecified models produce smooth, convex efficient frontiers, with Sharpe ratios degrading continuously rather than collapsing. This explains why modern machine-learning signals remain operationally useful despite model error. 

We then reinterpret portfolio allocation as a structured ensemble learning problem, where assets correspond to hypotheses and portfolio weights act as ensemble coefficients. Within this framework, diversification emerges naturally from the bias–variance–diversity trade-off, allowing risk diversification to be controlled ex-ante through model design rather than ex-post constraints.

Finally, we argue that while causality is not required for portfolio efficiency, it is essential for robust risk management. We introduce a causal driver and sensitivity-based framework that supports stress testing, regime analysis, and interpretable systematic risk control.

title: Can AI Be Energy Positive? Evaluating AI-Driven Efficiency in Industrial Manufacturing
affiliations: , ,  and University of California, Berkeley - Environmental Energy Technologies Division

detail.title: Can AI Be Energy Positive? Evaluating AI-Driven Efficiency in Industrial Manufacturing
detail.abstract: The growing energy demands of artificial intelligence (AI) systems have drawn increasing attention in recent years. However, the deployment of advanced AI technologies in manufacturing holds significant promise for improving efficiency, reducing costs, and enhancing sustainability, often surpassing the capabilities of traditional control systems such as programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and rule-based automation. By leveraging deep learning and predictive analytics, AI can optimize industrial processes, detect anomalies, and enable real-time decision-making. This study evaluates the net energy impact of AI in manufacturing through a comprehensive literature review and an industry-wide assessment. It examines the effects of AI technologies across various manufacturing sectors and cross-cutting utility systems, focusing on process parameters for optimization, energy efficiency improvement potential, additional environmental and non-energy impacts, relevant service providers, and deployment archetypes. The analysis also includes a dedicated case study on cement manufacturing, where advanced AI services are currently being commercialized. It evaluates energy savings in specific unit operations achieved through AI, as well as the electricity consumption of the supporting AI infrastructure, by modeling multiple server configurations and conducting a sensitivity analysis across various deployment scenarios. Despite ongoing concerns about AI's energy footprint, the findings suggest that its broader environmental and economic benefits in manufacturing far outweigh its associated energy use, potentially reducing primary energy demand and corresponding CO2 emissions by 4–13% in dry-process cement plants. These insights can inform future technology adoption strategies and support the development of effective policy frameworks.

title: From Enabler Psychology to Plutocratic Engineering: How Elite Psychological Capture, Rhetorical Norm Erosion, and Centurion Systems Convert Democratic Institutions to Wealth Concentration Mechanisms
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: From Enabler Psychology to Plutocratic Engineering: How Elite Psychological Capture, Rhetorical Norm Erosion, and Centurion Systems Convert Democratic Institutions to Wealth Concentration Mechanisms
detail.abstract:
This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical framework explaining democratic-to-oligarchic conversion in contemporary American politics through three integrated analytical levels. At the individual level, "enabler psychology" specifies the cognitive mechanisms through which educated political elites rationalize their transformation from democratic critics to authoritarian enablers, following a predictable four-phase progression (Initial Resistance → Gradual Accommodation → Sophisticated Defense → Institutional Enabling) facilitated by four psychological mechanisms: epistemic conditional compliance, constitutional conditional compliance, critical loyalism, and consequence shielding. At the operational level, "rhetorical forbearance breakdown" demonstrates how systematic rhetorical boundary erosion makes previously unthinkable constitutional violations appear reasonable, documented through empirical analysis of presidential term limit rhetoric escalation (2019-2025) culminating in 53% Republican voter support for constitutionally-prohibited third terms. At the system level, "centurion systems" theorize how functionally specialized elite networks coordinate individual psychological capture and rhetorical strategies into collective institutional transformation serving concentrated wealth interests.

The synthesis of these three levels reveals "plutocratic engineering"—the systematic conversion of democratic institutions into wealth concentration mechanisms through coordinated psychological capture of political elites, popular mobilization through engineered grievances, and institutional restructuring that amplifies concentrated wealth's political power while maintaining democratic legitimacy. This process operates through structural minoritarianism that amplifies minority political influence over democratic majorities, enabling policy outcomes opposed by popular majorities through procedurally legitimate mechanisms.

Drawing on cognitive dissonance theory (Festinger, 1957), motivated reasoning research (Kunda, 1990), democratic backsliding literature (Levitsky & Ziblatt, 2018; Bermeo, 2016), elite theory (Higley & Burton, 2006), and political economy research on wealth concentration (Piketty, 2014; Gilens & Page, 2014), this analysis provides crucial insights for understanding how democratic systems can be systematically converted to serve oligarchic rather than popular interests, with profound implications for democratic defense and institutional design.

title: Data-Driven Energy Management in the Steel Industry: Integrating Machine Learning with Operational Excellence Frameworks
affiliations: Kocaeli University

detail.title: Data-Driven Energy Management in the Steel Industry: Integrating Machine Learning with Operational Excellence Frameworks
detail.abstract: Energy-intensive industries, particularly steel manufacturing, play a pivotal role in global energy demand and carbon emissions, making operational energy efficiency a critical managerial and strategic concern. The steel sector, which accounts for approximately 7–9% of global CO2 emissions, faces persistent challenges to decarbonization because of its reliance on high-temperature thermochemical processes. This study adopts a data-driven management perspective to examine how operational parameters shape industrial energy consumption and how advanced analytics can support more effective energy management decisions.Using the Steel Industry Energy Consumption dataset, the study integrates exploratory data analysis, multivariate regression, and machine learning techniques—specifically the Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models—to analyze the nonlinear relationships between process variables and energy use. The findings demonstrate that furnace temperature, production rate, and material composition are the primary operational drivers of energy consumption. While linear regression provides baseline interpretability, machine learning models achieve substantially higher predictive accuracy, highlighting the limitations of traditional analytical approaches in complex industrial settings.From a managerial perspective, the study introduces the Industrial Energy Efficiency Index (IEEI) as a practical benchmarking tool that enables plant managers to compare actual energy consumption against predicted optimal levels for each operational cycle. The results suggest that significant improvements in energy efficiency can be achieved through operational optimization, production stability, and data-informed decision-making, rather than through capital-intensive technological upgrades alone.By empirically linking Lean Management, Total Quality Management (TQM), and Cleaner Production principles with machine-learning-based analytics, the study contributes to the strategic energy management literature and demonstrates how Industry 4.0-oriented digital tools can enhance operational efficiency and support industrial decarbonization efforts.

title: Fallible but improvable: Repeated evaluation reduces moral inconsistency
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE), London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Psychological and Behavioural Science and London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE)

detail.title: Fallible but improvable: Repeated evaluation reduces moral inconsistency
detail.abstract: Inconsistencies in people’s initial moral judgments are well-documented. How people address such inconsistencies when given an opportunity to reconsider their judgments has been less explored. Here, we examine whether people reduce inconsistency in their judgments on morally equivalent cases when given an opportunity to respond to the cases again. In particular, we study in which of three settings they are most likely to do so: (i) repeated separate evaluation; (ii) joint evaluation; and (iii) joint evaluation preceded by an explicit prompt to assess consistency. Using two exploratory studies, Pilot (N=148) and Study 1 (N=451), and a confirmatory experiment Study 2 (N=1,313), we find that repeated evaluation leads to a substantial reduction in inconsistency across all three settings. Participants are more likely to reduce their inconsistency under joint evaluation than under repeated separate evaluation. However, we do not find strong evidence that the addition of an explicit consistency prompt reduces inconsistency more than mere joint evaluation. Finally, while those who openly recognised their own inconsistency had a stronger tendency to reduce it, open recognition of inconsistency was neither sufficient nor necessary for reducing inconsistency. Our findings suggest that people’s moral judgments are fallible but improvable. Appropriate elicitation methods allow people to reduce inconsistencies in their initial judgments. However, our research also highlights that people’s pursuit of consistency is limited: many inconsistencies, even openly recognised ones, remained unresolved.

title: SA-Kmeans algorithm based polymerization control strategy for wide area distributed energy storage
affiliations: Yanshan University, Yanshan University, Yanshan University, Yanshan University and Yanshan University

detail.title: SA-Kmeans algorithm based polymerization control strategy for wide area distributed energy storage

keywords: Equalization evaluation function with adjustment factor

detail.abstract: A distributed energy storage grouping aggregation control strategy based on the SA-Kmeans algorithm has been proposed to address the operational path issues of charging and discharging multiple energy storage unit modules within a wide-area distributed energy storage system. To determine accurately the optimal number of clusters and the initial cluster center when using the Kmeans algorithm, the equalization evaluation function with adjustment factor and the SA-Kmeans algorithm are proposed to solve these two difficulties, respectively: The SA-Kmeans algorithm is used to cluster the SOC and power of the DESM (Distributed Energy Storage Modules), and an aggregate control strategy is formulated for the clustered operation. This aggregate control strategy not only achieves consistency in the SOC of each energy storage module, but also considers the power limit issue to ensure that the power of the energy storage module remains within the constraints. The clustering algorithm and the multicomponent polymerization control strategy proposed in this paper were verified using simulation examples, and the results show that compared with the traditional polymerization control algorithm, the method proposed in this paper has certain advantages in terms of the effect of module polymerization, consistency of the SOC of the energy storage module, and the number of charge and discharge operations.

title: Machine Learning Meets Markowitz
affiliations: Tongji University - School of Economics and Management, Tsinghua University - PBC School of Finance, Duke University - Fuqua School of Business, Tsinghua University and New Jersey Institute of Technology

detail.title: Machine Learning Meets Markowitz
detail.abstract: The standard approach to portfolio selection involves two stages: forecast the asset returns and then plug them into an optimizer. We argue that this separation is deeply problematic. The first stage treats cross-sectional prediction errors as equally important across all securities.  However, given that final portfolios might differ given distinct risk preferences and investment restrictions, the standard approach fails to recognize that the investor is not just concerned with the average forecast error - but the precision of the forecasts for the specific assets that are most important for their portfolio.  Hence, it is crucial to integrate the two stages, and this is the contribution of our paper. We propose a novel implementation utilizing machine learning tools that unifies the expected return generation process and the final optimized portfolio. Our empirical example provides convincing evidence that our end-to-end method outperforms the traditional two-stage approach.  In our framework, each investor has their own, endogenously determined, efficient frontier that depends on risk preferences, investor-specific constraints, as well as exposure to market frictions.

title: Coordinated electric vehicle evacuation with mobile charging stations: mixed-integer linear programming framework
affiliations: , , , , , University of California,  and University of California, Davis - Department of  Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

detail.title: Coordinated electric vehicle evacuation with mobile charging stations: mixed-integer linear programming framework
detail.abstract: As electric vehicle (EV) adoption increases, evacuating EVs during large-scale emergencies faces critical challenges in long charging times and limited charging infrastructure. This paper introduces mobile charging stations (MCS) as a flexible solution to facilitate evacuation. A mixed-integer linear programming framework is developed to model evacuation as a coordinated decision process, jointly optimizing route selection, vehicle grouping, departure scheduling, charging operations, and MCS locations. The framework accounts for heterogeneity in EV characteristics, including battery sizes and initial state-of-charge. A case study on Mariposa, California, shows that MCS deployment yields disproportionately large performance gains. Specifically, a 25% increase in charging capacity through MCS reduces maximum evacuation time by 33% and average waiting time by approximately 44% for heterogeneous EV populations. These gains result not only from added charging capacity, but also from improved utilization of existing infrastructure and new routing options enabled by MCSs, providing critical insights for EV evacuation planning.

title: Emergency Button: A Last-Resource Direct Load Curtailment Mechanism in the Netherlands
affiliations: TNO Energy-Transition, ,  and

detail.title: Emergency Button: A Last-Resource Direct Load Curtailment Mechanism in the Netherlands
detail.abstract: The transition toward a carbon-neutral Dutch economy relies heavily on end use electrification, particularly through the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and heat pumps. This increasing electricity demand poses challenges for the low-voltage grid, where congestion risks due to potential transformer overloading are expected to rise. While flexible resources can help mitigate these issues, their availability and responsiveness might not always be sufficient. This study investigates the potential role of an Emergency Button (EB) as a last-resort, direct load curtailment mechanism when other flexibility options are exhausted.The work combines a literature review of international emergency loadshedding programs with quantitative analysis using two custom tools: the Emergency Button tool, which estimates curtailment needs at the transformer level, and the Profile Generator, which models load and flexibility profiles based on copula theory. Results indicate that the need for EB activation depends primarily on the level of electrification, season, and available flexibility. Detached and post-war terraced houses show the highest likelihood of EB activation. Without such a mechanism, up to 45% of Dutch neighbourhoods could face transformer overloading by 2035. The study highlights the importance of defining the regulatory, technical, and social frameworks required to implement such emergency load-shedding measures in the Netherlands.

title: The Chronicles of Caspari: Should Caspari Expand Its Online Marketplace?
affiliations: University of Virginia - Darden School of Business, University of Virginia - Darden School of Business, ,  and University of Virginia - Darden School of Business

detail.title: The Chronicles of Caspari: Should Caspari Expand Its Online Marketplace?
detail.abstract:
In late 2024, Lisa Milbank, CEO and editor in chief of Caspari, Inc. (Caspari), a publisher of premium designed and printed paper products such as napkins, plates, gift wrap, and invitations, contemplated strategies to expand the company's market presence while preserving its artisanal heritage and high-end brand identity. Founded in 1945 as a European greeting card company, Caspari had evolved into a global brand known for collaborations with renowned artists and museums, with products sold primarily through wholesale channels to upscale retailers, grocery stores, and specialty shops. Although 75% of sales came from business-to-business (B2B) customers, online channels—including Caspari's Shopify-powered website (11% of sales) and Amazon.com (8%)—offered growth potential amid shifting consumer habits and e-commerce competition. Milbank weighed the risks of deeper Amazon integration, such as brand commoditization and loss of control, against opportunities to boost visibility and sales. Alternatives included doubling down on the company's own e-commerce site, opening more brick-and-mortar stores, or maintaining the status quo to focus on loyal, high-income customers and tactile in-store experiences. The case explores multichannel retail strategy, brand management, and digital transformation in a premium consumer goods market.This case is designed for use in courses on marketing strategy, e-commerce, or retail management. It provides opportunities for students to analyze distribution channels, competitive positioning, pricing, and promotional tactics, while also evaluating trade-offs between online expansion and brand integrity.

Excerpt

The Chronicles of Caspari: Should Caspari Expand Its Online Marketplace?

It was late 2024. Lisa Milbank, CEO and editor in chief at Caspari, Inc. (Caspari), the international publisher of designed and printed paper products such as napkins, plates, gift wrap, and invitations, sat down at her desk in the company's office in downtown Charlottesville, Virginia. It was a beautiful fall day, and the office was humming with activity. The team had recently returned from a proofing trip to Germany, overseeing the printing for the upcoming products that would fuel the holiday season's inventory and kick off the company's busiest time of year. Milbank reflected on her journey at Caspari, which had started serendipitously in 1981 in New York, where she'd been purely focused on leading design. Now she bore the weighty responsibility of guiding the company into its next era of growth. The question on her desk was: How should Caspari strategically expand its market presence to drive growth while preserving its premium brand identity and leveraging both online and offline channels?

Caspari's business was narrow yet unique. It featured exquisitely designed products in collaboration with globally renowned artists and museums such as the Royal Horticultural Society in England; the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston; and Colonial Williamsburg, Virginia. The company's most popular product categories—wrapping paper, paper napkins, and paper plates—were primarily sold wholesale to grocery stores and niche retailers such as specialty food stores, gift shops, and hardware stores, in both the United States and Europe. In an effort to elevate the everyday dining experience, Caspari often made paper plates in the trompe l'oeil style, so they appeared to be ceramic plates. Especially when compared to the cost of ceramic alternatives, Caspari's paper tabletop items were marketed at accessible price points—$5.95 for a package of cocktail napkins and $7.95 for paper plates.

While Caspari had thrived for decades based on its word-of-mouth legacy marketing, Milbank was now contemplating ways to bolster the brand's exposure to the online marketplace to increase sales. Embracing Amazon.com, Inc. (Amazon), the world's largest online retailer, was a viable option—but it also carried considerable risk. Caspari had sold some products on Amazon, and there was room to more fully lean in—but should it? Milbank wondered how Caspari could replicate its strong brand heritage and design expertise in an online context. Should Milbank view the Amazon marketplace as an opportunity to expand Caspari's reach or as a threat that could cannibalize its established high-end grocery, specialty, and retail channels? Should Caspari double down on selling through its own website? Milbank's thoughts went back to Caspari's strengths—leveraging its wholesale structure, cultivating loyal customers, and creating new products with original designs. Did growing its online presence risk damaging the brand? There was a lot to consider.
