title: Random Placement but Real Bias
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Random Placement but Real Bias

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Many studies exploit the random placement of individuals into groups such as schools or regions to estimate the effects of group-level variables on these individuals. Assuming a simple data generating process, we show that the typical estimate contains three components: the causal effect of interest, ”multiple-treatment bias” (MTB), and ”mobility bias” (MB). The extent of these biases depends on the interrelations of group-level variables and onward mobility. We develop a checklist that can be used to assess the relevance of the biases based on observable quantities. We apply this framework to novel administrative data on randomly placed refugees in Germany and confirm empirically that MTB and MB cannot be ignored. The biases can even switch the signs of estimates of popular grouplevel variables, despite random placement. We discuss implications for the literature and alternative “ideal experiments”.

title: From Skepticism to Support: Evidence-Based Insights for Priming Sustainability-Oriented Action
affiliations: and UNSW Sydney

detail.title: From Skepticism to Support: Evidence-Based Insights for Priming Sustainability-Oriented Action
detail.abstract: Environmental sustainability has moved from the margins to the core of strategic decision-making, yet many credible sustainability proposals still stall inside organizations. Even when the commercial case is strong, executives and boards frequently hesitate in the face of perceived risk, political signaling, or competing priorities. This article explains why internal persuasion around sustainability is so difficult and offers a practical framework for moving stakeholders from skepticism to support. Rather than focusing on public opinion or mass communication, we concentrate on firm-level decisions. Drawing on research in persuasion, judgment and decision-making, social identity, and moral psychology, we synthesize evidence into three clusters of barriers that commonly derail sustainability initiatives: time and risk biases (e.g., temporal discounting, loss aversion), identity and belief defenses (e.g., ideological conflict, motivated reasoning, obstinate personalities), and mechanisms of moral disengagement that mute guilt about potentially environmentally harmful decisions. For each barrier, we translate research into concrete rhetorical strategies that managers and directors can use when framing proposals, structuring decision processes, and shaping conversations. We then outline overarching implementation principles—disciplines of preparation, framing, and timing—that make these strategies more likely to succeed. The article’s contribution is both integrative and applied. It combines fragmented insights into a coherent, inside-the-firm persuasion toolkit and shows how leaders can use psychological science not only to understand resistance, but to design more effective paths toward sustainability-oriented action.

title: Determination of Best Practices for Sustainable and Energy-Efficient Production in Textile Dyeing Plants in Denizli Province, Türkiye: In Line with UN Sustainable Development Goals
affiliations: TUBITAK Marmara Research Center, TUBITAK Marmara Research Center, TUBITAK Marmara Research Center, TUBITAK Marmara Research Center, TUBITAK Marmara Research Center, TUBITAK Marmara Research Center, TUBITAK Marmara Research Center, VAT Enerji and Denizli Chamber of Industry

detail.title: Determination of Best Practices for Sustainable and Energy-Efficient Production in Textile Dyeing Plants in Denizli Province, Türkiye: In Line with UN Sustainable Development Goals
detail.abstract: Textile industries that involve dyeing and printing processes are characterized by their substantial energy consumption, which in turn results in considerable greenhouse gas emissions. This study was conducted in 40 different textile companies (38 dyehouses and 2 sizing plants) in Denizli, Türkiye. The specific energy consumption (SEC) of each plant was determined, and a benchmarking process was conducted using the Best Available Techniques (BATs) Reference Document (BREF) for the textiles industry, as well as existing literature. A comprehensive assessment of energy efficiency improvement techniques was carried out, including detailed evaluations of associated investment costs, anticipated annual energy savings, and payback periods. Furthermore, each identified technique was systematically aligned with the corresponding BATs outlined in the BREF document. The present study was conducted with the objective of evaluating economic and environmental gains relating BATs to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It was revealed that an annual energy saving of 12% and a revenue gain of 7.9 million euros could be achieved in 40 textile plants. The return of investments ranges from 0.7 to 3 years. Overall, the findings of this study suggest that textile plants can comply with BATs and contribute to SDGs 9, 12 and 13.

title: Forecasting with Log-Linear (S)VAR Models: Incorporating Annual Growth Rate Conditions
affiliations: Deutsche Bundesbank and Deutsche Bundesbank

detail.title: Forecasting with Log-Linear (S)VAR Models: Incorporating Annual Growth Rate Conditions
detail.abstract: This note explores conditional forecasting under conditions on annual growth rates, where variables enter a (possibly structural) vector autoregressive (VAR) model in logarithms or logarithmic first differences. For example, imposing conditions on the annual growth rate of quarterly real GDP modeled in logarithms is challenging because annual growth rates are nonlinear functions of the log variables. We address this by approximating the annual growth rate with a linear function of the model variables, enabling the use of standard conditional forecasting methods. An approximation error arises since the condition is not imposed directly; to mitigate this, we iteratively adjust the condition until the error is acceptable. We provide MATLAB companion code that also accepts other types of conditions: (1) conditions on the path of variables entering the VAR, (2) conditions on the path of structural shocks, and (3) conditions on sums of successive variable observations.

title: A Model Defense of Due Process Balancing
affiliations: Yeshiva University - Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law

detail.title: A Model Defense of Due Process Balancing
detail.abstract:
Judicial balancing has been subjected to a standard list of objections for decades, without anyone’s offering a comprehensive and persuasive response. This Article fills that gap. Balancing is not embedded in an invidious instrumentalism, such as utilitarianism, that saps law of its moral salience; it does not depend on the quantification or commensuration of manifestly qualitative legal interests; it is not arbitrary, result-oriented, or mere opinion; it does not invade the province of the legislature; and—most importantly—it does not risk balancing constitutional rights away by treating them as mere interests. 

The defense consists of a model. Models do not prove; they explain. A model-based defense is, therefore, a burden-shifting defense. If balancing can be modeled in a way that obviates the standard objections, then the burden is on balancing’s critics to show that their criticisms still stand.

The model of judicial balancing presented in this Article is based on an account of causal explanation in the sciences, known as a difference-maker account. A difference-maker account of causation is different from the counterfactual, but-for conception that lawyers use. The difference-maker account explains a phenomenon by eliminating some causal factors from the explanation, leaving only those necessary to represent it. A difference-maker model uses five connectives—inclusion, exclusion, abstraction, cohesive disjunction, and non-cohesive disjunction—to explain how the relevant causal factors are arranged to produce a minimum, maximally abstract explanation. This Article formulates a difference-maker model of Due Process balancing and uses it to provide a model-based, burden-shifting defense of the practice.

title: Labor Dispute Settlement Through Regional Trade Agreements: A Lesson from the North American Trade Bloc in Protecting Fair Labor Rights
affiliations: Michigan State University - College of Law

detail.title: Labor Dispute Settlement Through Regional Trade Agreements: A Lesson from the North American Trade Bloc in Protecting Fair Labor Rights
detail.abstract:
The past twenty-five years have seen a remarked increased in the interconnectedness between North America’s three largest economies—the United States, Canada, and Mexico. In response to this shift in national personality, the three nations renegotiated the agreement governing their trade relationship—the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA)—into the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement (USMCA). 

Along with a range of new and updated provisions, the USMCA took the remarkable step of obligating its signatory nations to meet the fair labor principles promulgated by the International Labour Organization (ILO). Chapter 23 of the USMCA, entitled “Labor,” requires parties to ensure their domestic labor laws protect worker’s fair labor rights, such as the rights to organize or collectively bargain. The USMCA also introduced a new mechanism for enforcing these obligations known as the Facility-Specific Rapid Response Labor Mechanism. The mechanism permits a party to bring a complaint and impose trade restrictions against a specific facility for a violation of that facility’s worker’s fair labor rights, and it requires a supra-national panel to issue binding resolutions on an expedited timeline. As of August 2024, the mechanism has been invoked on twenty-seven occasions. 

Learning from these successes, the world’s other mega-regional trade deals should institute similar labor obligations and enforcement mechanisms. The Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), which obligates parties to meet the fair labor principles of the ILO, should institute an enforcement mechanism for ensuring parties meet those obligations. Further, the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), which is the world’s largest trade agreement and devoid of any labor obligations, should reopen negotiations to institute a labor chapter and enforcement mechanism.

title: The Thrusts and Parries of Policy Arguments
affiliations: Boston University - School of Law

detail.title: The Thrusts and Parries of Policy Arguments
detail.abstract:
Anyone who has ever put forward a policy proposal has heard the response, "if it ain't broke, don't fix it." But despite the ubiquity of this attack on policy proposals, there has been little sustained inquiry into how the attack works and how it can be defended. The goal of this Article is to identify policy attacks like this, and to show their underlying logical structure, and how they function to attack policy proposals. The Article demonstrates this approach by considering three generic attacks on policy proposals, which I refer to as ain't broke attacks, partial framing attacks, and dollar in the street attacks. But these are just three particular ways that policy proposals can be attacked. To capture a broader set of policy attacks, the Article puts forward a general model of policy proposals, and the premises that they rely on. Since all policy proposals rely on these premises, all policy proposals can be undermined by rebutting these premises. The Article demonstrates the application of these attacks on three particular kinds of policy proposals: cost-benefit policy proposals, proposals for mandatory arrangements, and, what I refer to as Goldilocks proposals. 

By showing the thrusts and parries by which policy arguments can be attacked and defended, the Article aims to improve policy arguments. Modeling the structure of policy arguments abstracted from their particular contexts allows us to analyze them more deeply, and to amplify the benefits of that analysis for a broader set of applications. Identifying and labeling potential attacks on policy proposals facilitates responses to those proposals by others, and also allows authors to better defend against such attacks. Better policy arguments, both for and against, mean better policy debates, and therefore, better policy.

title: The Subscription Float: Recurring Revenue as Corporate Financing

detail.title: The Subscription Float: Recurring Revenue as Corporate Financing
detail.abstract: I study the rise of subscription revenue models and their implications for corporate finance. Using textual analysis of 2002–2023 SEC filings, I find that the share of firms citing subscription models has grown from 20.7% to 48.7%, and managers cite “revenue predictability” and “customer stickiness” as primary motivations. Exploiting within-firm adoption, I find that subscriptions reduce cash holdings by 2.3–2.6% of assets relative to firms’ pre-adoption baselines. This effect persists after controlling for cash-flow volatility and is associated with an 8.3–8.6% increase in asset growth. I argue that subscriptions function, in part, as customer financing: recurring payments create real options for the consumer, and, in turn, deferred revenue liabilities for the firm, decoupled from contemporaneous usage. This generates a customer-provided “float” that can, consistent with Einav et al. (2025), create usage-decoupled recurring revenue influenced by documented behavioral mechanisms. Using 2024 FTC regulatory actions, I estimate the portion of subscription firm value sensitive to changes in expected regulatory intervention targeting one such mechanism–cancellation frictions–at approximately 2%.

title: Reg BI+: Conflicted Sales Practices and Algorithmic Financial Advice
affiliations: Chicago-Kent College of Law - Illinois Institute of Technology

detail.title: Reg BI+: Conflicted Sales Practices and Algorithmic Financial Advice
detail.abstract:
Financial advisers are increasingly using advanced technology to provide more customized service. Yet these same technologies can shape the information retail investors receive and the choices they make-in ways that traditional financial regulation has not yet fully addressed. From the industry's perspective, the challenge is that many ordinary "retail" investors have a low willingness to pay for financial advice, meaning companies must cross-subsidize their production and may use technology to encourage investors to act in ways that may put the firm's interest ahead of the client's. 

In 2023, the SEC proposed a new "predictive data analytics" rule aimed at addressing these challenges, which has attracted heavy criticism from Wall Street. After describing the regulatory gap the proposal was meant to fill, this Article compares several alternative regulatory options and introduces the "Reg BI+ option." Under this regulatory alternative, certain parts of the existing framework would apply to these technology-mediated investor interactions. Rather than prohibiting conflicts like the SEC's proposed rule, the Reg BI+ option focuses on sales practices, and so would less directly challenge the revenue model under which broker-dealers solve the financing problem. 

This Article places the SEC's proposed rule within a broader context, reviews the details and legal basis for the proposal, and defends the Reg BI+ alternative. The Article's proposal would address the investor-protection harms that arise when people experience worse investment outcomes that result when they have been subjected to conflicted sales practices that put the adviser's interest first. In addition to discussing doctrinal tweaks to the proposal, this Article concludes with a discussion of the proposal’s approach to compliance, state-level fiduciary duty implications, and statutory interpretation in an era of increased judicial scrutiny of the SEC.

title: An APA for Tax
affiliations: University of Chicago - Law School

detail.title: An APA for Tax
detail.abstract:
Recent Supreme Court cases threaten to upend the administrative law applicable to the tax system. Loper Bright eliminates Chevron deference. Ohio v. EPA heightens the scrutiny given to regulatory preambles. And Corner Post effectively eliminates the statute of limitations for challenging the validity of regulations. A number of lower court decisions move in the same direction, aggressively using administrative law to invalidate guidance. Combined, these decisions threaten to make issuing guidance much more difficult and to slow the guidance process. 

These decisions are based on the Administrative Procedure Act or related statutes rather than constitutional principles. Therefore, to the extent that they are bad policy or are inappropriate readings of the applicable statutes, they can be changed. To this end, this Article explores what an Administrative Procedure Act for the tax system might look like. It considers six issues that have been at the forefront of the application of administrative law and closely related areas of law to tax: (1) arbitrary and capricious review, mostly focusing on its application to regulatory preambles; (2) the statute of limitations for challenging the validity of a regulation; (3) the standard of deference to Treasury regulations; (4) the method of interpreting tax statutes; (5) the requirement to use notice and comment; and (6) the use of temporary regulations. In each case, this Article considers the relevant policy issues and recommends an administrative procedure tailored to the needs of the tax system (without asking whether similar changes are needed elsewhere).

title: When Gender Kicks In: An Experimental Study of Work from Home and Attitudes to Household Work and Childcare
affiliations: University of Oslo - Ragnar Frisch Centre for Economic Research, Oslo and Akershus University College - Oslo Metropolitan University, University of Toulouse I - GREMAQ & LIRHE, Paris School of Economics (PSE) and Tilburg University, Netspar

detail.title: When Gender Kicks In: An Experimental Study of Work from Home and Attitudes to Household Work and Childcare

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how working from home links to gendered attitudes about household work and childcare. Using a vignette experiment embedded in a regular Dutch population representative survey, we randomly vary the gender of the partner working from home in a hypothetical dual-earner couple. When presented with various routine and emergency chores, respondents, on average, agree that the partner working from home should execute them. These effects are significantly larger when the vignette randomly depicts a man, rather than a woman, working from home, but these gender differences in respondents’ expectations vanish in a scenario where no partner works from home. All in all, the evidence gathered indicates that Work from Home may blast rather than boost gender norms around household work and childcare.

title: Moral Dury or "Mere Can't"? Tax Protesting Through the Looking Glass
affiliations: Duke University School of Law

detail.title: Moral Dury or "Mere Can't"? Tax Protesting Through the Looking Glass
detail.abstract: In a recent New York Times op–ed, Princeton University sociologist Matthew Desmond proposed an innovative form of tax protest—intentionally overpaying one’s federal income tax by choosing not to claim deductions and credits to which one is legally entitled, as a way of registering one’s policy objection to the unclaimed tax benefit.3 Although this tax protest technique could be used against a wide range of deductions and credits, Desmond’s oped paid particular attention to the home mortgage interest deduction, which he criticized as a “ridiculous deduction,” which serves as “primarily a windfall for the wealthy,” and the benefits of which disproportionately “flow to white households.” Although Desmond praises another taxpayer (Alejandro Narvaez, a Seattle dentist) who intentionally foregoes deductions to which he is entitled but to which he objects on policy grounds, Desmond explains that his own family has registered its objection in a different way—”by donating what we receive from the mortgage-interest deduction to affordable housing initiatives on top of our regular giving.” His bottom line: “I honestly don’t know if it’s better to donate tax deductions or, like Mr. Narvaez, refuse them outright. I only know that it feels unfair to keep it all for ourselves.” His hope is that, if enough Americans follow his lead— either by intentionally foregoing objectionable deductions or by donating to charity the tax savings from objectionable deductions claimed—those taxpayers would “send Washington a clear message that they would support progressive tax reform by enacting such reforms in their own lives.” Although one might reasonably be skeptical of the prospects of persuading a meaningful number of Americans to renounce tax breaks to which they are legally entitled, of the six letters the Times published a few days later in response to Desmond’s op–ed, five supported one or both version of Desmond’s proposal. In this Article, I explore Desmond’s proposal from several angles. The question is whether there is a compelling case for Desmond’s proposed tax protest movement or whether his claim that affluent taxpayers benefitting from various tax breaks have a moral duty to overpay their taxes by foregoing the tax breaks is, in Learned Hand’s words, “mere cant.” Part I of the Article situates the proposal in a long line of tax protest movements—mostly movements refusing to pay taxes legally owed, but also a few antecedents to Desmond’s protest-by-overpayment. Part II considers whether there are any legal constraints on taxpayers intentionally overstating their own tax liabilities. It explains there are some constraints, but not enough to close off this avenue of protest. Part III offers several reasons why, even assuming legality and a taxpayer broadly in sympathy with Desmond’s views on social justice, a taxpayer might want to think twice (at least) before deciding to follow Desmond’s lead. The basic point is that, viewed in the context of the overall tax structure, few if any tax breaks are so clearly unfair that a taxpayer should feel morally compelled to forswear them, even if the taxpayer would happily support their repeal.

title: Resilient Hybrid Air-Ground Networks for Disaster Preparedness and Response: A Distributionally Robust Approach
affiliations: ,  and Peking University

detail.title: Resilient Hybrid Air-Ground Networks for Disaster Preparedness and Response: A Distributionally Robust Approach
detail.abstract: Disaster relief operations are frequently paralyzed by substantial network failures that sever access to affected regions during the critical "golden period". While traditional logistics rely on ground transport and strategic airlift, their effectiveness can be compromised by correlated infrastructure collapse or airport bottlenecks. This paper proposes a resilient network design framework integrating decisions with facility location, inventory pre-positioning, and contingent airlift leasing. Motivated by the prohibitive ownership costs of such assets, we model the acquisition of tactical capacity (eVTOLs) through contingent contracts, enabling a flexible response. We formulate the problem as a two-stage distributionally robust optimization model with a Wasserstein ambiguity set to hedge against the joint uncertainty of demand and network connectivity when data are sparse. For computational tractability, we derive an equivalent reformulation and solve it via generalized Benders decomposition. Comparative analysis of the Yushu earthquake and the U.S. hurricane season reveals that the optimal investment portfolio is highly dependent on the disruption topology. In scenarios with fine-grained disruptions, the tactical capacity functions as essential lifeline bridges to bypass ground failures. Conversely, under coarse-grained spatial uncertainty, the model prioritizes facility dispersion and strategic airlift to extend the efficiency. The proposed framework demonstrates endogenous scale adaptability, effectively quantifying the trade-off between static robustness and dynamic flexibility.

title: Trade Restrictions as Effective Industrial Policy? Evidence from Indonesia's Import Licensing Scheme
affiliations: Jaume I University,  and

detail.title: Trade Restrictions as Effective Industrial Policy? Evidence from Indonesia's Import Licensing Scheme
detail.abstract: Industrial policy is on the rise. A key instrument used by governments is import licensing to protect domestic industries. However, evidence of its effectiveness is limited. Using customs and firm level data, we estimate the effects of the introduction of import licensing for iron and steel products in Indonesia in 2009. While we find that the number of incoming shipments of protected products is reduced, and that imports are sourced from fewer countries, the overall value or quantity of imports is not affected. At the same time, while domestic iron and steel producers increase their sales in the short run, we do not find long-lasting positive effects on their sales. Our results suggest that while import licensing imposes costs on importers who have to adjust their supply chains, sustained gains for domestic producers are limited. This suggests that import licensing is ineffective as an industrial policy.

detail.abstract: This study explores the public narratives surrounding Sherly Tjoanda, the Governor of North Maluku, during October 2025, employing a qualitative descriptive approach with narrative analysis. Data were collected from viral content on online media and social platforms, including YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, and local news portals. The narratives are grouped into six thematic clusters: participatory efficiency and digital governance, public spending priorities, anti-corruption and governance transparency, economic legitimacy, gender and leadership representation, and sustainability versus extractive industry. The analysis reveals that Sherly's leadership is perceived through a dual lens: innovation in participatory governance and tension in public accountability. Her actions-rejecting a Rp1.7 billion budget proposal for manual road surveys, prioritizing direct citizen reporting via social media, and emphasizing education-health spendingreflect an effort to modernize governance while maintaining fiscal efficiency. Yet, public debates around transparency, wealth, and the mining sector reveal how narratives of trust and legitimacy remain fragile in local administration. Interpreted through theories of public administration such as public value, accountability, and governance of complexity, this study emphasizes that female leadership in regional governance is not only about representation, but also about redefining bureaucratic responsiveness in a society shaped by algorithmic public opinion.

title: Underrepresentation Bias in Clinical Trials: The Ripple Effect on Medical Decision-Making and Patient Outcomes
affiliations: , Indiana University - Kelley School of Business and Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Operation & Decision Technologies

detail.title: Underrepresentation Bias in Clinical Trials: The Ripple Effect on Medical Decision-Making and Patient Outcomes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no financial, personal, or professional relationships, affiliations, or interests that could be perceived as influencing the work reported in this manuscript.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any funding.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: While high-quality clinical trials remain the gold standard of medical decision-making, the low enrollment of specific populations relative to their disease burden may compromise healthcare delivery. This paper studies how underrepresentation bias in clinical trials affects physician decision-making and patient outcomes. Methodology/results: We propose a dual process model to analyze physicians' treatment decisions, which are influenced by two distinct cognitive systems: the rational and the intuitive systems. The rational system is modeled as a multi-armed bandit problem with Bayesian updating, whereas the intuitive system is modeled using a "win-stay, lose-shift" heuristic. We aim to explore whether these decision-making systems worsen healthcare outcomes by relying on biased clinical trial results or if they adapt to mitigate underrepresentation bias by learning from actual patient outcomes. We find that while the rational system correctly identifies the optimal treatment when the new treatment is less effective, it may not converge to the optimal treatment when a new, more effective treatment is introduced. In contrast, the dual process system corrects the impact of the bias under some conditions regarding the intuitive system. This result suggests that the intuitive system based on simple heuristics may compensate for the rational system's incomplete learning through sufficient exploration of treatment options. We also conduct a case study to explore how women's underrepresentation in clinical trials ripples through physician decision-making to cause poor healthcare outcomes, including unnecessary low-dose aspirin prescriptions for myocardial infarction prevention and missed prevention of ischemic stroke. Managerial implications: The findings suggest that when a subgroup is known to be underrepresented in clinical trials, focusing more on the treatment outcomes relative to the clinical trials helps accelerate learning, thus reducing disease incidence and treatment-related side effects. However, the corrective effect of this learning can vary significantly among different diseases.

keywords.keywords: Optimal Control; Finite Dimensional Control;Differential Games; Evolutionary Dynamics; Stochastic Optimal Control; Rare events

detail.abstract: We develop a comprehensive mathematical framework for adaptive cancer therapy using rigorous optimal control theory, differential game theory, and stochastic analysis. Traditional maximum tolerated dose (MTD) protocols fail to account for evolutionary dynamics and competitive release of resistant populations. We formulate adaptive therapy as a class of optimal control problems on evolutionary game-theoretic models, prove existence and characterization results for optimal strategies, and extend the framework to stochastic settings with rare resistance emergence. The project combines deep results from viscosity solution theory, mean-field games, large deviation theory, and measure-valued stochastic processes to establish a mathematically rigorous foundation for evolutionary therapy design.

title: Corporate Presence and Charitable Giving: Evidence from Panel Data on Firms and Nonprofits
affiliations: SUNY University at Albany,  and

detail.title: Corporate Presence and Charitable Giving: Evidence from Panel Data on Firms and Nonprofits
detail.abstract: The interconnectedness of activities in and between the corporate, government, and nonprofit sectors continues to garner considerable attention in academic and public policy debates. The degree to which the presence of one sector generates positive spillovers to other sectors and thus local economies is of particular interest. In this paper, we examine specifically how the presence of corporate firms is associated with nonprofit, charitable activity in US metropolitan areas. We find evidence of a positive association consistent with Card, Hallock, and Moretti (2010) and, due to a longer time horizon with additional information on nonprofit activity, are able to provide additional investigation into how firm location affects size of the nonprofit sector and other nonprofit activities such as fundraising. Our estimates suggest a lower bound on the spillovers such that the presence of an additional firm headquarters within a metropolitan statistical area (MSA) leads to a $8.2 million increase in total charitable contributions within the same MSA. Moreover, a $1 billion rise in the aggregate market value of firms within an MSA corresponds to a $0.8 million increase in local charitable donations. We additionally find evidence that more corporate activity is associated with increased nonprofit fundraising expenditures and more active charities. Importantly, we detect no significant impact of corporate headquarters on government grants received, nor do we find significant evidence of crowding out effects of public contributions on government grants to local charities. These findings offer better understanding of the interplay between private sector growth and nonprofit sector dynamics, shedding light on the economic mechanisms that shape local philanthropic landscapes.

title: Analysis of Teachers’ Code of Ethics Violations
affiliations: Universitas Cokroaminoto Palopo and Universitas Cokroaminoto Palopo

detail.title: Analysis of Teachers’ Code of Ethics Violations
detail.abstract: The teacher’s code of ethics serves as a moral and professional guideline for educators to maintain integrity, responsibility, and the quality of educational services. However, various violations in Indonesia show that its implementation still faces significant challenges. This paper analyzes several forms of code of ethics violations, including physical and verbal violence, harassment, grade manipulation, discrimination, and abuse of authority. The contributing factors are examined from the internal aspects of teachers, school environment, and weak regulatory enforcement. The impacts on students, schools, and the teaching profession are also discussed. Real-life case studies are presented to illustrate the complexity of issues found in the field. This paper further proposes recommendations such as strengthening ethics education, improving supervision, enforcing strict sanctions, providing professional support for teachers, and fostering an ethical school culture. These efforts are expected to reduce violations of the teacher’s code of ethics and promote sustainable teacher professionalism.

detail.abstract: This working paper critically examines the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR) licensing regime for issuers of asset-referenced tokens (ARTs), comparing it with other regimes in EU financial regulation, and also in relation to other jurisdictions. MiCAR approach to ARTs issuers licensing, in fact, reflects the hybrid nature of ART issuers-as issuers and intermediaries (in particular, e-money institutions and money market mutual funds)-and some level of EU regulator's distrust and concern for stability towards this new type of entities, reflected in the higher level of discretion of NCAs in their authorisation decision and the frequent reference to stability and monetary sovereign in this context. The resulting special regime is a patchwork of different financial regulation regimes, which however never assimilates ART issuers to "traditional" issuers/intermediaries or ARTs to private/public money. The paper concludes by evidencing the main critical issues for the functioning of this new regime.

detail.title: Risk Analysis and Competitiveness Assessment of the South Korean Military Aircraft Supply Chain

publicationDetails.detailsText: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade Research Paper No. 25/MER/10/01
publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
South Korea’s defense exports have continued to grow steadily, driven by the strong performance of major programs such as the FA-50 light attack aircraft and the second export batch of the K2 main battle tank (MBT). At the same time, supply chain risks have intensified due to US–China trade tensions, rising raw material prices, and embargoes on Russian inputs. 

Against this backdrop of fragmenting global supply chains, we analyzed the supply chain for Korea’s military aircraft and identified major risk factors. For the FA-50 program, we classified and evaluated 52 defense contractors based on systems specialty (avionics, propulsion, fuselage, and components) and evaluated their financial performance, dependence on imports, and reliance on Korea’s main systems integrator, Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI). T

We also performed a comparative case study contrasting the FA-50 program with Italy’s M-346/FA program. This analysis shows that the FA-50 benefits from a stable and reliable procurement network. But this network is heavily concentrated in the United States and a small group of countries; the supply chain for the M-346/FA is more resilient thanks to its more diversified sourcing.

The results of the analysis carry three strategic implications for Korea’s military aircraft industry.

First, there is a clear need to pursue technological self-reliance in avionics and propulsion systems by localizing major links in the supply chain. Second, the supply chain features a large number of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs); efforts are needed to enhance the competitiveness of these firms. Finally, it is critical to expand the participation of fuselage and components suppliers in global value chains. Integrating these priorities within a coherent supply chain governance framework is essential to stabilizing production, safeguarding technological resilience, and enhancing Korea’s competitiveness in the global defense market.

title: Moral Values and Social Norms
affiliations: and

detail.title: Moral Values and Social Norms
detail.abstract: This paper discusses the essential role of moral values and social norms in shaping individual behavior and maintaining order within society. Moral values function as internal principles that guide individuals in distinguishing right from wrong, while social norms serve as external rules collectively agreed upon to regulate behavior in accordance with shared values. Both concepts are closely interconnected, as moral values become the foundation for the establishment of social norms that operate in everyday life. This paper explains the definitions, characteristics, and functions of moral values and social norms, along with practical examples of their implementation, particularly in school settings where character development is emphasized. Furthermore, the paper highlights the negative consequences that may arise when these values and norms are neglected, including deviant behavior, weakened social cohesion, and declining moral character among younger generations. Overall, this study emphasizes the importance of collaboration between families, schools, and communities in consistently instilling moral values and social norms to support the formation of responsible and ethical individuals.

title: Large Language Models as Independent Reasoning Systems Co-Evaluating a Bistable Theory of Cognitive Switching

detail.title: Large Language Models as Independent Reasoning Systems Co-Evaluating a Bistable Theory of Cognitive Switching
detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a newly accessible way to evaluate theoretical coherence, yet their potential role as independent reasoning systems remains unexplored. This paper tests whether three distinct LLMs—Claude, Gemini, and GPT—converge on the same internal mechanism when reasoning about a theoretical account of the analytic evaluative cognitive transition. The theory proposes a bistable switching process characterized by threshold behavior, collapse regions, asymmetric transitions, and recognition-based recovery. Each model was prompted separately, using varied wording and without access to the formal machinery of the theory. Across sessions, the models independently reconstructed structural features resembling the proposed bistable architecture, including instability boundaries, nonlinear transitions, and recognition-like reorganization. Divergences across models revealed characteristic inferential styles, but convergence on core structural elements suggests that the mechanism contains internal constraints strong enough to be rediscovered by independent systems. The findings demonstrate that LLMs can serve as early-stage theoretical evaluators, identifying latent structure, failure modes, and mechanistic boundary conditions. Although LLM convergence is not empirical validation, it provides a novel methodological tool for assessing theoretical coherence. The study illustrates how LLMs may complement traditional theory-building by revealing which aspects of a proposed model are structurally necessary, overdetermined, or underspecified.

title: A Brief Analysis of the Japanese Sovereign Debt Market

detail.title: A Brief Analysis of the Japanese Sovereign Debt Market
detail.abstract: This paper examines the sustainability and market implications of Japan’s unusually high sovereign debt, which remains above 200% of GDP on a gross basis but is closer to 156% on a net basis once internal public-sector holdings are included. It traces how the post‑Plaza Accord asset bubble and subsequent fiscal expansions created today’s debt overhang, then analyzes the current ownership structure, highlighting the dominant role of the Bank of Japan and domestic financial institutions and the limited exposure to foreign holders. The paper argues that this configuration reduces classic external default risk but heightens sensitivity to inflation expectations, term premia, and yen moves as the BOJ exits ultra‑loose policy and the Takaichi administration deploys debt‑financed stimulus. It links these dynamics to recent increases in 10‑ and 20‑year JGB yields and pressures on the BOJ’s balance sheet, and briefly outlines relative‑value implications for global investors considering JGBs versus alternatives such as Indian and Swiss sovereign debt.

title: Two-Pizza Teams and Rapid Experimentation: Reconfiguring Organizational Strategy for Innovation in the Digital Economy

detail.title: Two-Pizza Teams and Rapid Experimentation: Reconfiguring Organizational Strategy for Innovation in the Digital Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patients, or the collection of primary personal data. The research is based on a conceptual and theory-building approach using secondary data from published literature and publicly available documented organizational practices (Amazon’s two-pizza teams). As no direct interaction with individuals occurred, formal ethics committee approval was not required. No written informed consent was necessary for this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the nature of Amazon's "two-pizza" team model, as an organizational design that institutionalizes rapid experimentation, dynamic capabilities, and ambidexterity in day-today work in the digital economy. The concept integrates and focuses existing theoretical approaches such as dynamic capabilities, the lean startup approach, organizational ambidexterity, team autonomy and complexity theory to build a model that explains how small cross-functional teams and disciplined experimentation routines interact to influence innovation performance and operational performance. From a methodological stance, the paper adopts a narrative and theory-building approach that combines existing literature on microprocesses of digital innovation with an analytical case study (i.e., Amazon's two-pizza teams), using recorded practices such as single-threaded leadership, multidisciplinary independence, and data-based experimentation. The analysis reveals how two-pizza teams function as micro-foundations of sensing, seizing and transforming activities that facilitate rapid product iteration, strategic optionality, and structural ambidexterity but create coordination risks, knowledge fragmentation and autonomy paradoxes at scale. Based on these insights, the paper introduces a new organizing scheme that connects four key constructs of team structures, experiments routines, enabling context and performance outcomes through non-linear relationship lines which are moderated by culture, leadership and digital infrastructure. The paper concludes that the two-pizza model is a powerful but context-dependent design pattern: while it can greatly accelerate innovation and learning in digitally intense organizations with supportive culture and infrastructure, significant attention needs to be paid to calibrating autonomy, governance, and experimentation vehicles in heavily regulated or capital-intensive industries.

title: An Examination of Corporate Risk of the Forbes-Just Capital 100 for 2018
affiliations: Pepperdine University, Pepperdine University - Graziadio School of Business and Management and Pepperdine University - Graziadio School of Business and Management

detail.title: An Examination of Corporate Risk of the Forbes-Just Capital 100 for 2018
detail.abstract: Investment portfolios were constructed from the S&P 500 companies listed in the Forbes-Just Capital 100 for 2018. This list implies that the inclusion of ESG/DEI goals in such portfolios should lead to maximizing corporate wealth with less corporate risk. The constructed portfolio contained 19 stocks, which remained in the Forbes-Just Capital 100 list for each year of the fiveyear period under study. Results from this exploratory study indicate that, contrary to prior assertions, these such focused portfolios did not show a statistically significant change in their risk characteristics, as measured by unadjusted beta and unadjusted alpha, over a five-year period. The study results suggest serious consideration should be given to questioning the inclusion of ESG/DEI goals in corporate strategic decision-making and in the construction of investment portfolios.

title: EMBEDDING RESILIENCE IN BIO-BASED PRODUCTION THROUGH FUNCTIONAL MODULARITY: A MIXED-METHOD APPROACH
affiliations: Nha Trang University, Nha Trang University and Nha Trang University

detail.title: EMBEDDING RESILIENCE IN BIO-BASED PRODUCTION THROUGH FUNCTIONAL MODULARITY: A MIXED-METHOD APPROACH
detail.abstract: Resilience in bio-based production systems is often treated as a reactive response rather than an embedded structural property. Drawing on shrimp farming in Vietnam, this study reconceptualises functional modularity as a design principle that internalises resilience within production architecture. A sequential mixed-methods approach combines an in-depth case study, which reveals how modular structures localise disturbances and stabilise operations, with a quasi-experimental analysis that quantifies the causal impact of modularity on production continuity during pandemic shocks. Results show that resilience arises endogenously from the spatial and temporal configuration of separable modules while reducing costs. The study advances theory by positioning modularity as a generative structural property, identifies the mechanisms that produce resilience, and clarifies the conditions for its effective implementation, offering guidance for designing resilient bio-based production systems under multiple, simultaneous risks.

title: Reforming America's High-Skilled Immigration: Evidence-Based Policy for Global Competitiveness
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: Reforming America's High-Skilled Immigration: Evidence-Based Policy for Global Competitiveness
detail.abstract: The United States faces mounting competitive pressure in global talent markets due to structural deficiencies in its high-skilled immigration system. This study examines the H-1B visa program's performance against domestic workforce challenges and international alternatives, revealing systematic disadvantages that undermine American competitiveness. Using comparative analysis of immigration systems in Canada, Australia, Germany, and Singapore, alongside empirical data on program outcomes, this research demonstrates that lottery-based allocation, processing uncertainty, and unclear permanent residency pathways drive qualified candidates to competitor nations. The analysis proposes evidence-based reforms including merit-based allocation, strategic government oversight, accelerated permanent residency pathways, and regional distribution mechanisms. These recommendations address domestic workforce development concerns while enhancing America's ability to attract and retain global talent.

title: Information Management in Risk Cultures: Toward a Theory of Risk Information Culture

detail.title: Information Management in Risk Cultures: Toward a Theory of Risk Information Culture

keywords: risk management Information Management in Risk Cultures: Toward a Theory of Risk Information Culture

detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly operate in what has come to be recognized as a volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous environment, where threats materialize rapidly, risks propagate through tightly coupled systems, and the signals of failure are ambiguous or obscured. Effective risk management therefore depends upon the quality of the information that organizations generate, share, interpret, and utilize as they confront uncertainty. This paper argues that an organization's ability to anticipate hazards and respond to emerging threats is deeply shaped by its risk information culture, defined here as the set of values, norms, and practices that govern how risk-related information is sought, interpreted, communicated, and used. We review the foundational research on the central role of information and information management in risk management and based on this review, we propose a typology of four risk information culture types: Reliabilityfocused, Innovation-oriented, Performance-driven, and Compliance-directed. Each type is discussed in terms of its underlying values, dominant information practices, interpretive tendencies, and implications for risk governance. The proposed typology could serve as a research framework and as a practical tool to profile risk information cultures, allowing organizations to identify strengths and weaknesses in their risk management strategies, and to improve their risk information management.

title: Effects of rating systems on platform markets: monopolistic competition approach
affiliations: Kanagawa University - Faculty of Economics and Kochi University of Technology

detail.title: Effects of rating systems on platform markets: monopolistic competition approach
detail.abstract: In platform markets, rating systems are essential in alleviating uncertainty of products' quality and attracting consumers to the marketplace.  We examined the effects of a rating system on sellers' entry into and exit from a platform market characterized by monopolistic competition. We focused on the fact that the accuracy of a rating system affects the distribution of the products' expected qualities in the marketplace. In the model, we assumed that the platform controls the quality distribution in a monopolistic competitive market.Given the number of sellers (products), a more accurate rating system designed by the platform always benefits consumers. By contrast, in a free-entry environment, a more accurate rating system pushes out lower-quality sellers. This shrinks the variety of products and may decrease the consumer surplus and the platform's revenue.We provide some necessary and sufficient conditions for such decreases to occur.In addition, when improving the accuracy of the rating system does not incur additional costs, the platform sets a rating accuracy that favors consumers (rather than sellers). Otherwise, the platform underprovides the accuracy of the rating system.

title: TRIBES: Twin-Driven Resilient and Intelligent Blockchain-Enabled Security Framework for UAV Swarms
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing Institute of Technology, Inner Mongolia Agricultural University, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing Institute of Technology, Inner Mongolia Agricultural University and Beijing Institute of Technology

detail.title: TRIBES: Twin-Driven Resilient and Intelligent Blockchain-Enabled Security Framework for UAV Swarms
detail.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms operating in contested environments must achieve secure coordination, perform real-time fault detection and containment, and enforce operational policies under conditions of dynamic membership and hostile interference. However, existing approaches remain limited to addressing singular and specific issues, failing to provide a comprehensive, unified system security framework. We present TRIBES, a modular four-layer trust framework that unifies distributed consensus, online anomaly detection with the Digital Twin (DT) technique, privacy-preserving attestation, and resilient dual-path communications without centralized infrastructure. The architecture anchors a lightweight Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) ledger with a reconfigurable Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) committee, achieving sub-second finality in typical operation. Simulation studies with realistic swarm dynamics under spoofing, jamming, and Sybil attacks demonstrate that TRIBES sustains auditable trust decisions with low tail latency, while DTs detect compromised behavior with high accuracy and few false alarms. Privacy is preserved through differential perturbation and simulated zero-knowledge attestations, enabling on-chain enforcement of geofencing and other operational policies. Compared with decentralized baselines, TRIBES reduces worst-case consensus latency by about one-third and maintains swarm coordination even under targeted disruption.

title: RegOps4RailML: Embedding Compliance Governance in Railway Interoperability Architectures
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: RegOps4RailML: Embedding Compliance Governance in Railway Interoperability Architectures
detail.abstract: The increasing digitalization of railway operations has heightened the importance of interoperable data exchange standards such as RailML. While RailML ensures syntactic and semantic consistency across railway information systems, it lacks integrated mechanisms for regulatory governance and compliance assurance---capabilities essential for safety-critical environments. This paper introduces the RegOps4RailML framework, a RegOps-enabled architecture that embeds continuous regulatory oversight directly into the RailML lifecycle. The framework defines a regulated lifecycle---draft, validate, approve, publish, and archive---supported by verifiable metadata, digital approvals, and automated audit generation. The proposed architecture demonstrates how compliance can become a continuous and verifiable property of data interoperability systems, transforming regulatory assurance into an integral architectural concern. By treating RailML artifacts as regulated entities, the approach bridges the gap between technical validation and regulatory accountability, aligning data exchanges with standards such as EN 50128 and EN 50129. A dedicated XML Schema Definition (RegOps4RailML) and instance files demonstrate the feasibility of embedding governance metadata within RailML structures. A qualitative evaluation shows that the proposed framework enhances traceability, auditability, and trustworthiness while preserving interoperability, providing a foundation for continuous compliance and transparent governance in digital railway ecosystems.

title: A Centralized ICT-Driven Planning Cockpit for Real-Time Multi-Supplier Collaboration and Commitment Integration in ERP Systems

detail.title: A Centralized ICT-Driven Planning Cockpit for Real-Time Multi-Supplier Collaboration and Commitment Integration in ERP Systems
detail.abstract: This paper proposes an innovative ICT-based framework for real-time collaborative forecasting in ERP-integrated supply chains, addressing limitations in traditional systems such as delayed supplier engagement and disconnected commitment capture. The core artifact is a centralized planning cockpit—an orchestration module that integrates internal demand signals with parallel supplier inputs via secure, standardized interfaces, enabling dynamic commitment feedback on quantities, pricing, and delivery schedules directly linked to procurement execution.Adopting a design science research methodology, the framework extends existing ERP collaborative modules by introducing structured multi-supplier engagement mechanisms and automated forecast-to-procurement conversion logic. Scenario-based evaluation, informed by industry implementations, demonstrates the cockpit's enabling capabilities in reducing process latency, enhancing real-time visibility, and minimizing manual interventions.Results indicate noticeable improvements in planning efficiency and supplier coordination, offering a generalized approach for leveraging ICT to bridge forecasting and execution in complex industrial networks, providing actionable insights for enhancing transparency and agility. This work highlights emerging practices in ICT-enabled collaborative work systems within ERP environments, providing actionable insights for improving transparency and execution readiness in industrial supply chains.

title: Delete Sequence Data for Educational Platforms: Machine Unlearning in Knowledge Tracing Model
affiliations: University of Bergen, Monash University,  and Monash University

detail.title: Delete Sequence Data for Educational Platforms: Machine Unlearning in Knowledge Tracing Model
detail.abstract: With the proliferation of adaptive learning systems powered by Knowledge Tracing (KT) models, massive sequential student interaction data are collected to enable personalized education. However, privacy regulations such as GDPR and CCPA mandate the "right to be forgotten," requiring the complete removal of individual data from trained models, a challenge unaddressed by simple database deletion due to persistent model memorization. Retraining from scratch is computationally pro- hibitive, prompting the need for efficient Machine Unlearning (MU) in KT. This paper presents the first systematic investigation of MU in KT models operating on sequential educational data. We evaluate three representative MU methods across different KT models in real-world datasets under diverse deletion scenarios. Re- sults show that Gradient Ascent strikes a superior trade-off between efficiency and unlearning efficacy, while surprisingly, retraining does not always achieve perfect for- getting accuracy, revealing residual influences in sequential data. Furthermore, we uncover that forgetting difficulty is not simply correlated with sequence length or skill diversity, but modulated by model architecture, deletion granularity, and data entanglement. These findings challenge intuitive assumptions and provide action- able insights for developing KT-specific unlearning strategies in privacy-compliant educational platforms.

title: Hear to Reveal: Stealing Keystroke Content from Keyboard Acoustic Side-Channel
affiliations: , , , ,  and Jinan University

detail.title: Hear to Reveal: Stealing Keystroke Content from Keyboard Acoustic Side-Channel
detail.abstract: With the widespread application of high-precision microphones in various smart terminals, attackers can eavesdrop on users' keystroke content. Although existing attack strategies have made some progress in specific scenarios, they generally face practical application bottlenecks such as insufficient generalization ability and strong dependence on environment and data. To reveal the real threat of attacks based on sound signals, we propose a method for stealing keystroke content from the acoustic side-channel on keyboards, named HERO. First, we improve the ability of detecting keystroke fragments from complex backgrounds through a multi-scale energy fusion strategy. Then, through self-supervised pre-training using spectral masking and feature reconstruction, HERO learns key representations from keystroke audio. Finally, we guide HERO to learn the distinguishing keystroke features based on discrimination tasks. In particular, the labeled keystroke samples are used to improve HERO's classification performance in the fine-tuning stage. Extensive experiments covering various mainstream keyboards demonstrate that our proposed HERO outperforms existing baselines on multiple evaluation metrics. Its robustness is further verified by varying noise levels, recording distance, recording position, and microphone type. In real-world scenarios, HERO achieves 97.5% accuracy in word input tasks and 93% accuracy in numeric password input tasks. Under a strict leave-one-out protocol with 10 participants, HERO achieves 90.5% average accuracy, demonstrating its strong cross-user generalization ability. These results validate HERO's adaptability and theft effectiveness in real-world environments, highlighting the serious threat that keyboard acoustic side-channel attacks pose to user privacy.

title: Architectural Fusion for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comparative Framework
affiliations: University of Tehran, Sharif University of Technology and University of Qom

detail.title: Architectural Fusion for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comparative Framework
detail.abstract: Despite significant advances in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), no single architecture consistently outperforms others across all query types and evaluation criteria, especially in fact-sensitive, regulatory domains. We address this by introducing a structured taxonomy of advanced RAG methods, grouping them into three families: Query Enhancement, Retrieval and Context Enrichment, and Graph-Enhanced RAG (GraphRAG). We evaluate nine representative variants on a challenging benchmark of 500 queries from Sharif University’s official regulations, using a human-validated, multi-dimensional LLM-as-a-Judge framework across seven quality dimensions. Results show clear trade-offs: GraphRAG excels in factual accuracy and grounding; context enrichment methods (e.g., Raptor) lead in relevance and helpfulness; query enhancement favors fluency but sacrifices source fidelity. Critically, we propose a novel analytical framework, using pairwise overlap analysis and the average max score, to quantify functional complementarity. We find that RAG families exhibit largely non-overlapping failure modes, enabling oracle ensembles to boost correctness by up to +1.47 over the best single system. This provides strong evidence for Fusion RAG: dynamically combining complementary architectures to maximize robustness. We outline a roadmap for adaptive routing, efficiency analysis, and cross-domain validation to advance ensemble-based RAG in real-world applications.

title: Understanding Experiences of Data Literacy Through Dali Life
affiliations: Coventry University, Coventry University, Coventry University and University of the Balearic Islands

detail.title: Understanding Experiences of Data Literacy Through Dali Life
detail.abstract: In the post-digital era, proliferation of data necessitates strong data literacy for active citizenship. Educators, policymakers, and technologists advocate for skills to empower citizens in navigating, evaluating, and utilising data environments. This paper presents the design and evaluation of Dali Life, a game which enhances citizens ability to comprehend, evaluate, and mitigate risks associated with data usage. Employing game-based research complimented by mixed methods involving adult participants (n=84), the study investigates citizen’s experiences of interacting with Dali Life, exploring how game elements influence data literacy perceptions and practices.  The research also investigates broader implications of employing games as pedagogical tools for advancing data literacy. Findings indicate that relatable, meaningful scenarios significantly enhance participant engagement and facilitate deeper understanding. Two critical dimensions emerged as vital to nurturing data literacy: (1) conceptual understanding of data literacy and (2) meaningful engagement with data-driven scenarios. These dimensions transcend the traditional technical discourse of data literacy, encouraging participants to construct cognitive frameworks and skills necessary for addressing data-related challenges. The insights gained from this study contribute to both theoretical and practical knowledge, informing experts and data literacy advocates on leveraging game-based interventions to foster civic competencies, social innovation, and practical problem-solving capabilities in everyday contexts.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Project Performance Monitoring: A Data-Driven Framework for Predictive and Real-Time Insights
affiliations: and

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Project Performance Monitoring: A Data-Driven Framework for Predictive and Real-Time Insights
detail.abstract: Project performance monitoring has continued as a challenge across industries, as most current methodologies still depend on historical indicators or domain-specific digital tools that are not able to provide predictive and real-time insights. While artificial intelligence and machine learning offer new opportunities, current frameworks remain fragmented, which limits their use for project control to be proactive. This study addresses this gap by proposing a unified AI-based data-driven framework for predictive and real-time monitoring. Adopting a design science research approach, this study conducts a systematic literature review to analyse traditional project monitoring frameworks, digital real-time systems, AI-based conceptual models, and predictive machine learning approaches. Insights from this review are considered to develop the design requirements that guide the development of this proposed framework. A conceptual evaluation was undertaken through criteria-based comparison and scenario-based reasoning, analysing existing frameworks based on key factors such as the ability to predict, real-time responsiveness, dimensional completeness, cross-sector applicability, and operational maturity. The analysis revealed that no existing frameworks have provided the complete integration of predictive analytics with real-time monitoring across several performance dimensions. The proposed framework addresses these limitations by incorporating machine learning-based prediction, continuous data integration, and decision-support mechanisms with a unified architecture. This study provides a theoretically grounded and conceptually evaluated framework that offers a foundation for future empirical validation and practical AI-supported project performance monitoring implementation.

title: Why Licensing Lacks Its Own Metadata System: A Practitioner-Scholar Examination of Data Fragmentation and the Need for a Unified SKU-Level Licensing Intelligence Infrastructure in the $369B Global Consumer Products Industry

detail.title: Why Licensing Lacks Its Own Metadata System: A Practitioner-Scholar Examination of Data Fragmentation and the Need for a Unified SKU-Level Licensing Intelligence Infrastructure in the $369B Global Consumer Products Industry

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical Considerations The system did not record any information about individual consumers. The research data originates from publicly accessible product listings and packaging information and corporate disclosure materials. The mystery shopping activities followed all rules which the platform had established in its terms of service. The research fails to reveal any studio-owned proprietary systems which operate as internal licensing platforms.

detail.abstract: The worldwide consumer products licensing industry which generates $369 billion in value lacks a single metadata system to track and authenticate licensed products throughout different product segments and geographic markets. The licensing sector operates without an official system which provides standardized identifiers for IP-intensive sectors to use such as ISBN and ISRC and DOI. The lack of data collection leads to multiple problems which include data fragmentation across different territories and the loss of data to other regions and the entry of counterfeit products and problems with royalty payment records. The research investigates structural factors which create metadata gaps through a three-year study which involved fans and mystery online shoppers and distributed volunteers who performed manual SKU verification. The research analyzed more than 40,000 licensed SKUs together with hundreds of global licensees which provided scientists with unusual opportunities to study product expansion and market reactions. The research results show that information access between licensors and licensees and retailers and digital platforms and enforcement bodies creates a widespread knowledge gap which contradicts conventional beliefs about licensing transparency and compliance. The research demonstrates that a single licensing intelligence system which uses real-time SKU information and verified licensee lists and digital territory monitoring technology would create better IP protection and precise royalty payment systems and improved customer confidence. The practitioner–scholar lens shows how real-world operations affect theoretical aspects which produce valuable insights for intellectual property management and anti-counterfeiting policy development and digital commerce governance and future global licensing system modernization.

title: Value Proposition and Revenue Model in On-demand Insurtech
affiliations: University of Tehran, Faculty of Entrepreneurship, University of Tehran, University of Tehran and University of Tehran

detail.title: Value Proposition and Revenue Model in On-demand Insurtech
detail.abstract: Despite the utility of on-demand insurtech as an emerging phenomenon, it faces significant acceptance challenges among stakeholders and has failed to become institutionalized. This radical innovation lacks legitimacy; as long as it is not perceived as simple and comprehensible by its audience and fails to meet their expectations, its adoption will encounter substantial difficulties. Thus, a precise understanding of stakeholder expectations and the design of a business model aligned with these demands are essential for the institutionalization and rapid diffusion of this innovation. Accordingly, the present study aims to identify and analyze the value proposition and revenue model components, and to propose suggestions for achieving coherence between them. This research is an applied study employing a qualitative-survey approach. Data were collected via semi-structured interviews with 27 experts, drawn from both the insurance industry and the technology sector. Data analysis was conducted using content analysis with a grounded theory coding approach. The study's findings include 48 categories pertaining to the revenue model, value proposition, and the suggestions for integrating these two components. The key conclusion of this research highlights the necessity of establishing new pricing criteria and balancing the preferences of customers and insurers within the business model elements of on-demand insurtechs.

title: How to Design an AI Agent: Architectures, Protocols, and Technical Evaluation of Agentic AI Systems for Law & Finance
affiliations: 273 Ventures, Illinois Tech - Chicago Kent College of Law and 273 Ventures

detail.title: How to Design an AI Agent: Architectures, Protocols, and Technical Evaluation of Agentic AI Systems for Law & Finance
detail.abstract: Agents are not magic; they are architecture. In high-stakes domains like law and finance, the difference between a reliable tool and a runaway process lies in design. This chapter focuses on the architectural principles required to allow agents to function as cognitive work systems analogous to, and in concert with, professional teams.  We organize our analysis around ten fundamental questions that shape an agent's operational reality. These range from input mechanisms (triggers, intent, perception, and memory) to execution strategies (planning, delegation, and action tools). Crucially, we examine the safety layers required for professional deployment: termination conditions, human escalation protocols, and governance.  Behind each of these ten questions lies a design decision with real tradeoffs. These choices determine what a system can do, how reliably it performs, and how it fails. Ultimately, this chapter argues that robust design requires architectural literacy—a necessary bridge between technical implementation and professional obligation.
